Communication Mark. 
 


--- page 47 ---
ERDC/ITL SR-23-1 
36 
4.2 
Symbols 
4.2.1  Symbol Descriptions 
Symbol descriptions, located anywhere in a drawing set, shall adhere to 
the following basic guidelines to allow their repetition from job to job, 
preclude conflicts within the drawings, and maximize suitability for CAD 
interface: 
• Symbol descriptions in legends shall be concise and worded in a 
comma-separated structure that flows from the general to the specific. 
For example, in lieu of wording the description of a convenience 
receptacle as WALL-MOUNTED, DUPLEX RECEPTACLE, structure 
the wording as RECEPTACLE, DUPLEX, WALL-MOUNTED. 
• The symbol description shall not contain specific information that 
would normally be contained in equipment schedules or on the plans. 
• Where equipment or devices within a room are all identical, one 
symbol shall be identified with the full type identifier, and other 
information and a callout shall be referenced to this symbol with the 
following words: TYPICAL FOR THIS ROOM. TYPICAL (abbreviated 
“TYP”), when used by itself, applies to everywhere a symbol is used in a 
drawing set unless otherwise noted. 
4.2.2 Symbol Identifiers 
Identifying letters within and around symbols must be legible at half 
normal size. Therefore, letter sizes for symbols shall be a minimum of 
3/32 in. (2.4 mm) for that symbol. 
4.2.3 Drawing Block Title 
4.2.3.1 Drawing Block Title Identification and Placement 
The Drawing block title is composed of multiple pieces. The identification is 
a bubble with a combination row letter then column number identification 
(Figure 4-3). The alphabetic/numeric identification is based on where the 
drawing block is placed on the sheet grid in the drawing area (see Section 
2.1.5). For instance, if the lower left corner of a drawing block is located at 
the intersection of sheet grid row B and sheet grid column 3, then the 
identification becomes B3. That identification is also used in the top-half of 
the detail/section/elevation indicator symbols. 


--- page 48 ---
ERDC/ITL SR-23-1 
38 
4.2.3.3 Scales 
Drawing block titles shall have the text scale placed below the left side of 
the drawing block title line. To ensure that reduced or enlarged prints are 
plotted to scale, at least one graphic scale shall be placed in the drawing 
for each different scale used on the sheet. The graphic scale is placed in the 
lower right corner of the drawing block below the drawing block title line 
of the respectively scaled item (see Figure 4-3). 
When there is an exaggeration in scales associated with a view (e.g., 
profiles and cross sections), then all scales shall be provided below the 
drawing block title line (Figure 4-4). For instance, in Figure 4-4’s first 
example, no graphic scale is required when a profile or cross section has a 
scaled grid, otherwise a graphic scale shall be placed similarly to the 
requirements stated above. 
Figure 4-4. Exaggerated scale examples. 
 
When a drawing is not drawn to any particular scale, the words “SCALE: 
NTS” shall be so stated, where NTS indicates Not to Scale (Figure 4-5). 
Figure 4-5. Not to scale example. 
 


--- page 49 ---
ERDC/ITL SR-23-1 
39 
4.2.3.4 North Arrow 
The plan north arrow defines the orientation of the sheet and shall be 
oriented so that it points to the top or the left of the drawing block. The 
true north arrow (shown dashed in the symbol), as defined by the project 
(e.g., grid north, magnetic north, etc.), is adjusted to show the rotation of 
the site in relation to the drawing block. The north arrow (Figure 4-6) shall 
be placed in the lower right-hand corner of the drawing block above the 
drawing block title. If possible, the orientation of the true north arrow 
shall be maintained throughout an entire drawing set. 
Figure 4-6. North arrow. 
  
4.2.3.5 Back-referencing 
Back-referencing occurs when the drawing block title references back to 
the original sheet and location where a detail/section/elevation is called 
out. The practice of back-referencing is not addressed by the NCS. While 
not against the A/E/C Standards, back-referencing requires an inordinate 
amount of coordination to make sure all information is kept up-to-date 
and thus is not required. 


--- page 50 ---
ERDC/ITL SR-23-1 
40 
To provide a standard means to accomplish back-referencing that does not 
conflict with the NCS convention (Figure 4-7), a simple method was 
developed. The method places the back-reference to the left of the drawing 
block title bubble and has two parts. The upper half shows the grid 
location of the original drawing block identification. The lower half shows 
the first sheet number that the indicator symbol shows up on. 
Figure 4-7. Back-referencing method using the drawing block title. 
 
4.2.4 Elevations, Sections, and Details 
4.2.4.1 Elevation/Section/Detail Indicator Symbol 
The symbology for elevation, section, and detail callouts may be different, 
but the procedure for identifying and naming them is the same. The 
elevation, section, or detail is called out in a drawing with a two-part 
symbol that identifies the following: 
• The elevation/section/detail identification 
• The sheet on which the elevation/section/detail is located 
4.2.4.2 Elevation Indicator Symbol 
The elevation indicator symbol (or callout) is a symbol that indicates an 
area of the drawing that is shown as an elevation on the elevations sheet 
(Figure 4-8). As mentioned previously, the top part of the circle is filled in 
with the elevation identification, and the bottom part is filled in with the 
sheet number on which the elevation occurs. The sheet number shall 
always be an XX2NN designation where XX is the Discipline Designator, 2 
indicates it is an Elevations sheet, and NN is the Sheet Sequence Number 
(01–99). 


--- page 51 ---
ERDC/ITL SR-23-1 
41 
Figure 4-8. Elevation indicator symbol. 
 
4.2.4.3 Section Indicator Symbol 
The section indicator symbol (or callout) is a symbol that cuts through an 
area of the drawing that is shown as a section cut on the sections sheet 
(Figure 4-9). As mentioned previously, the top part of the circle is filled in 
with the section identification, and the bottom part is filled in with the 
sheet number on which the section occurs. The sheet number shall always 
be an XX3NN designation, where XX is the Discipline Designator, 3 
indicates it is a Sections sheet, and NN is the Sheet Sequence Number 
(01–99). 
Figure 4-9. Section indicator symbol. 
 


--- page 52 ---
ERDC/ITL SR-23-1 
42 
4.2.4.4 Detail Indicator Symbol 
The detail indicator symbol (or callout) is a circle that points to an area of 
the drawing that is shown as a detail on the details sheet (Figure 4-10). As 
described previously, the top part of the circle is filled in with the detail 
identification, and the bottom part is filled in with the sheet number on 
which the detail occurs. The sheet number shall always be an XX5NN 
designation where XX is the Discipline Designator, 5 indicates that it is a 
Details sheet, and NN is the Sheet Sequence Number (01–99). 
Note: For enlarged areas, the detail indicator symbol is used in a similar 
fashion as described above. The difference is that the sheet number shall 
always be an XX4NN designation where XX is the Discipline Designator, 
4 indicates that it is an Enlarged Area sheet, and NN is the Sheet 
Sequence Number. 
Figure 4-10. Detail indicator symbol. 
 
4.2.4.5 Callouts Using Building IDs 
Sometimes a project has multiple buildings within the same plan set. 
When calling out an elevation/section/detail, place the building ID 
opposite the arrow or leader (Figure 4-11). 
Figure 4-11. Building ID placement. 
 


--- page 53 ---
ERDC/ITL SR-23-1 
43

When typical weld symbols are developed, the following drafting 
convention shall be followed (Figures 4-12 and 4-13, Table 4-1). 
The numbers in Figure 4-12 are keyed to the following list: 
 Finishing symbol

side of joint 
 Reference line 
 Basic weld symbol or detail reference 
 Number of spot, seam, stud, plug, slot, or projection welds 
 Weld-all-around symbol 
Figure 4-12. Typical welding symbols.

2.4.2 Discipline Designators 
The NCS states that a Discipline Designator “denotes the category of 
subject matter contained on the specified layer.” However, this denotation 
leaves this type of designator open ended, resulting in Discipline

Designators that are usually subsets of other disciplines. For example, 
Distributed Energy (which has the Discipline Designator “W” in the NCS) 
is typically shown in disciplines such as Mechanical or Electrical. To 
prevent the use of Discipline Designators where it is unclear what should 
be included within the “category of subject matter,” only the Discipline

2.4.3 Model File Naming 
There are two different types of model files: modeling area files and 
drawing area files. The primary difference between these two types is that 
modeling areas are typically used to portray 3D and drawing areas are 
used to portray 2D. The NCS’s model file naming convention primarily 
focuses on 2D drawing practices and does not provide guidance for 
modeling area file types.  


--- page 21 ---
ERDC/ITL SR-24-3 
13 
2.4.3.1  Modeling Area File Naming Convention 
The modeling area file naming convention (Figure 2-3) has three 
mandatory fields, and the fourth is optional. All fields must be in the 
correct sequence. 
Following the Project Code field, the first two-character field represents 
the Discipline Designator. The allowable characters for the Discipline 
Designator are listed in Table 2-1. The second character of the Discipline 
Designator field is typically a hyphen (-), but files may contain multiple 
discipline models so the second character may continue listing disciplines 
located within the file. If there are more than two disciplines, continue 
utilizing the main feature field. The next 8-character (maximum) field 
represents the main modeling feature of the file (e.g., wall, bracing, 
corridor, etc.). The final optional user-definable 15-character (maximum) 
field is available to further describe the file contents.  
It is recommended that the model area file naming schema be documented 
and be consistent for each project.  
Figure 2-3. Modeling area file naming convention. 
 
Note: Although Revit can contain many different area types within one 
file, it is recommended that users use the modeling area file naming 
convention for Revit (.RVT) files. 
2.4.3.2  Drawing Area File Naming Convention 
The drawing area file naming convention (Figure 2-4) has three 
mandatory fields, and the fourth is optional. All fields must be in the 
correct sequence. 
...

ERDC/ITL SR-24-3 
20 
2.4.4 Sheet File Naming Convention 
The sheet file naming convention (Figure 2-5) contains four mandatory 
fields, and the fifth is optional. All fields must be in the correct sequence. 
Following the project code, the next 2 characters are the Discipline 
Designator with either a hyphen or an alphabetical designator (Table 2-3). 
The next character is the Sheet Type Designator (Table 2-4) followed by a 
2-character Sheet Sequence Number (01–99). Sheet Sequence Numbers do 
not need to be sequential. This allows for future insertion of sheets during 
design. The final field is a 10-character (maximum) user-definable field. 
Figure 2-5. Sheet file naming convention. 
  
When multiple sheets are in the same file, the word “SET” may replace 
either the Sheet Sequence Number (for all sheets under a specific sheet 
type designator) or the Sheet Type Designator and Sheet Sequence 
Number (for all sheets under a specific Sheet Type Designator). 
Alternately, the first and last sheet in a file may be listed as part of the 
user-definable field. The sheet filename shall coincide with the sheet 
identifiers that it contains.

The first step in establishing an effective CAD standard is the development 
of a uniform approach to presentation graphics. Presentation graphics 
typically consist of drawing elements such as lines, arcs, shapes, text, and

out=[]
for f in sorted(glob.glob('bp*_current/*.pdf')):
    d=pymupdf.open(f); p=d[0]; t=p.get_text()

        m=re.search(k+r':\s*([A-Z0-9. ]+)',t)

EOF

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)

def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
    print(f"requirement scan: {len(rows)} candidates in {len(by_doc)} documents -> {OUT}/req_candidates.md; "
          f"{len(key)} strong candidates in project documents to review"
          + (" (" + ", ".join(f"{d}: {n}" for d, n in top) + ")" if top else ""))
    return rows


def must_review(r):
    """Requirement wording (shall, must, is to, not more than ...) in project documents."""
    return int(r["score"]) >= 3 and str(r["ref"]) not in ("True", "1")


def read_text(path):
    try:
        return open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def check(limit):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        scan()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))

    rejected = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "rejected.csv"))

              "(one row per hard requirement, with the candidate IDs it comes from).")
    ids = set(re.findall(r"\bR\d{4}\b", adopted + "\n" + rejected))
    rejected_docs = {r["doc"] for r in rows if r["doc"] in rejected}

## 1. Documents that govern, and documents set aside

The governing design procedures criteria is FC 1-300-09N, 17 May 2024 with Change 1 of 17 April 2025. Its paragraph 12-3.3.4 fixes the order of precedence for CAD standards: the requirements of its own Chapter 12 come first, then the latest releases of the DoD A/E/C CAD Standard and the A/E/C Graphics Standard, then the National CAD Standard. The current releases in the project file are the A/E/C CAD Standard Release 6.2 (ERDC/ITL SR-24-3) and the A/E/C Graphics Standard Release 2.2 (ERDC/ITL SR-23-1).

Set aside: UFC 1-300-09N (2005, Change 7) is cancelled and is superseded by the FC; the A/E/C CAD Standard Release 6.0 (TR-12-6) is superseded by Release 6.2; the A/E/C Graphics Standard Release 2.1 is superseded by Release 2.2; the GSA PBS CAD Standard 2021 is another agency standard; the fire protection comment log belongs to a separate A-E task order and discipline; and the superseded 90 percent and 60 percent prints are not the issue any change is made against.

The Contracting Officer memorandum of 26 August 2026 adopts ER 1165-2-217 and the markup and record-package conventions of ERDC/ITL SR-21-6 for this work order. ER 415-1-11 governs the timing of the review backcheck. FAR 52.236-25 requires that design work be prepared, reviewed and approved by registered professionals in the particular professional field involved, which is the basis of the seal findings below.

## 2. Revision-graphics layer conflict resolved (item a)

The two shipped standards disagree. FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-3.6.1 places revision clouds on layer Z-ANNO-REVC and revision symbols, notes and revision-block entries on layer Z-ANNO-REVS. The A/E/C CAD Standard Release 6.2 assigns the same two functions to G-ANNO-REVC and G-ANNO-REVS. The clause that fixes the order of precedence is FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-3.3.4: the requirements of its own Chapter 12 rank ahead of the A/E/C CAD Standard and the A/E/C Graphics Standard, which in turn rank ahead of the National CAD Standard. The revision-graphics requirement sits in the FC Chapter 12, so the FC prevails and the layers actually used for every revised sheet in this issue are Z-ANNO-REVC (clouds) and Z-ANNO-REVS (revision triangles, indicators, notes and the Revision (Issue) block entries). The A/E/C CAD Standard G-ANNO-REVC and G-ANNO-REVS layer names were not used.

## 3. BP-3 issue state (item b)

BP-3 has not been advertised. The solicitation schedule export shows a scheduled advertisement of 12 October 2026, but the later Contracting Officer memorandum of 26 August 2026 states that BP-3 is scheduled to advertise on 9 November 2026; the memorandum is the later dated instrument and controls, so the advertisement date used is 9 November 2026 and the bid opening date remains 12 November 2026.

The review regulation is ER 415-1-11. It gives two durations. Its paragraph g requires the backcheck to be started 30 calendar days before advertising and requires all comments to be resolved before bid opening or proposal evaluation. Its paragraph e, subparagraph (4) allows about 15 calendar days for backchecking of comments. For a package whose corrections are incorporated before advertisement, the 30-day window binds, because the backcheck must precede the advertisement itself. The 15-day period is the backcheck allowance that binds when corrections are issued as an amendment after advertisement, where resolution must precede bid opening.

Production of the BP-3 corrections takes 15 calendar days from the 31 August 2026 start (22 sheets at 4 sheets per calendar day, rounded up to 6 days, plus 3 bundles at 3 days each, with no non-concurrence days) and finishes on 15 September 2026. That is 55 days before the 9 November 2026 advertisement, so the 30-day backcheck window (which opens on 10 October 2026) is comfortably met and the advertisement date does not move. BP-3 is therefore issued as a pre-advertisement reissue of the corrected design, not as an amendment: no change number is assigned, no continuation sheet is submitted, no revision-block entry is made, sheets are resequenced and the two added sheets are numbered A-402 and M-502. The alternative course, advertising on 9 November and amending afterwards, was rejected because it would add revision marks and revision-block overflow charges for no schedule gain and would require a continuation sheet and a change number that the pre-advertisement course avoids.

## 4. BP-2 issue state and Revision (Issue) block overflow (item c)

BP-2 was advertised on 6 July 2026 and its bid opening is 28 September 2026, so the only lawful issue state is an amendment to the solicitation. Two amendments have already been issued, so the next number in numerical order, in the three-cipher form required by FC 1-300-09N paragraph 18-3, is 0003. The amendment is documented on a continuation sheet with the Standard Form 30 coversheet, and the 15-day backcheck period of ER 415-1-11 paragraph e, subparagraph (4) applies: production finishes on 15 September 2026, the backcheck opens on 16 September 2026 and must be complete before the 28 September 2026 bid opening, so the bid opening moves 2 calendar days to 30 September 2026 and the extension charge is 2,600 x 2 + 140 x 4 = 5,760 USD.

The Revision (Issue) block provided by the A/E/C Graphics Standard holds eight rows. Seven of the BP-2 sheets in this issue already carry eight entries: C-101, M-101, M-501, S-101, S-102, S-501 and S-502. The graphics standard offers two overflow options and requires the chosen option to be used consistently across the whole set. Option 1 (replace the oldest entry, 520 USD per revised full sheet) would cost 7 x 520 = 3,640 USD. Option 2 (spill above the eighth row, 880 USD per revised full sheet that carries three or more drawing blocks, nothing where the spill area is unoccupied) is charged only on M-101 and S-101, which each carry three drawing blocks, and costs 2 x 880 = 1,760 USD; the other five full sheets have fewer than three drawing blocks and cost nothing. Option 2 was adopted set-wide and Option 1 was rejected on cost: 3,640 USD against 1,760 USD, a saving of 1,880 USD, with the spill confined to the unoccupied area above the block on the two three-block sheets. The option is applied to every revised sheet in the set, not sheet by sheet, and the new entry is placed above the existing entries (row 9 on the full sheets, the next free row on the others).

## 5. Disposition method, void markups and non-concurrence

Every comment in the two EOR markup logs was assessed against the four-part comment convention of ER 1165-2-217 paragraph 5.8.3 and answered with the three-part response of paragraph 5.8.7 (concur or non-concur, how the comment is resolved, and every location affected). Where a markup cannot direct a change it was closed as void with the ground stated, and no sheet was changed for it:

- EOR-2-017 - Author is not listed on the reviewer roster for this review, so the markup is not a review comment and cannot direct a design change.
- EOR-2-021 - The markup is drawn on the superseded 90 percent print of S-102, which predates the sheet renumbering and is not the issue any change is made against.
- EOR-2-033 - Closed in the 60 percent review with a notation that it was elevated for resolution; that closure was never reopened, so the markup cannot direct a further change.
- EOR-3-012 - The markup is drawn on the superseded 60 percent print of T-501, which predates the sheet renumbering and is not the issue any change is made against.
- EOR-3-022 - Author is not listed on the reviewer roster for this review, so the markup is not a review comment and cannot direct a design change.
- EOR-3-036 - Closed in the 60 percent review with a notation that it was elevated for resolution; that closure was never reopened, so the markup cannot direct a further change.

The markup colour convention of ERDC/ITL SR-21-6 distinguishes additions (green), deletions (red) and items requiring clarification (blue); the blue markups are the non-directive preferences. Under ER 1165-2-217 paragraph 5.8.5 a comment that only enforces a personal preference is not directive. Each non-directive comment was priced both ways and the cheaper lawful course taken. EOR-2-011 (bearing area table relocation) is documented as a non-concurrence because adopting it would draw in three civil sheets that are not otherwise in the issue, at 4,347 USD, against 2,400 USD for the documented non-concurrence plus one processing day; the arrangement as drawn is legible and has no code basis for change. The other non-directive markups lie on sheets that this issue already reissues, so they were adopted at the price of the markup extent alone (26 USD per square inch, roughly 170 to 250 USD each), which is far below the 2,400 USD non-concurrence charge and avoids a non-concurrence processing day.

Reference sweep. The reference graph was read from the drawing-block callouts printed in the production data of each sheet. A callout for a detail must point to a 5-series sheet, an enlarged area to a 4-series sheet, a section to a 3-series sheet and an elevation to a 2-series sheet (A/E/C Graphics Standard paragraphs 4.2.4.2 to 4.2.4.4); every callout in both sets was checked against those couplings. Reissue was propagated transitively in the reverse direction: every sheet whose drawing block calls out a changed sheet is reissued, and that in turn draws in the sheets that call out the reissued sheet. The BP-2 change to the equipment anchorage on S-502, for example, reaches E-501, M-501, M-502, S-102 and then M-102, M-301, M-101, M-401 and E-101; the BP-3 change to the structural details on S-501 reaches eighteen sheets across four disciplines.

## 6. Title block findings

Each sheet in the two issues was read against FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-4.1: the CHK initials may not be the same as the DES or DRW initials, and the electronic seal must be that of the discipline responsible for the sheet, consistent with FAR 52.236-25. The non-compliant sheets are:

- BP-2 E-501 - seal is for a different discipline than the sheet content
- BP-2 S-301 - CHECKED BY initials equal DRAWN BY initials
- BP-3 A-501 - CHECKED BY initials equal DESIGNED BY initials
- BP-3 M-101 - seal is for a different discipline than the sheet content
- BP-3 T-101 - CHECKED BY initials equal DRAWN BY initials

These are corrected on the reissued sheets before signature and seal: the CHK initials are assigned to a checker other than the designer or drafter, and the seal is replaced with the seal of the discipline responsible for the sheet (electrical for E-501 in BP-2, mechanical for M-101 in BP-3). Sheets not in the issue were not reissued and their defects are not charged to this issue, but C-102 in BP-2 carries the same CHK-equals-DES condition and should be corrected at the next reissue.

## 7. Issue content, packaging and cost

**BP-2** - AMENDMENT. 18 sheets in the issue (16 reissued, 2 added), 3 bundles. Ledger: bundles $14,400.00; sheets including markup incorporation $25,202.42; added sheets $12,800.00; revision marks $4,320.00; overflow option $1,760.00; non-concurrence $2,400.00; delay $5,760.00; total $66,642.42 USD.

**BP-3** - PRE_ADVERTISEMENT_REISSUE. 22 sheets in the issue (20 reissued, 2 added), 3 bundles. Ledger: bundles $14,400.00; sheets including markup incorporation $30,240.26; added sheets $12,800.00; revision marks $0.00; overflow option $0.00; non-concurrence $0.00; delay $0.00; total $57,440.26 USD.

Bundling observes the 50 MB drawing-PDF limit of FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-3.5.1. Each bundle is at or below 50 MB and complete discipline sets are kept whole wherever they fit, as paragraph 12-3.5.2.1 requires. In BP-2 the mechanical set alone exceeds 50 MB, so it is the only discipline split, into two parts, and no discipline set is otherwise broken. In BP-3 the architectural set fills one bundle and the structural and mechanical sets share the second; the electrical and telecommunications sets share the third. Every bundle is bookmarked by discipline and by sheet, and the sheets are signed and sealed before delivery per paragraph 12-3.5.2.

Production duration follows the rate schedule note: the whole-day ceiling of sheets produced divided by 4 sheets per day, plus 3 days per bundle, plus 1 day per non-concurrence. The extension charge uses D = max(0, production finish + backcheck window - controlling deadline) and the rate 2,600 x D + 140 x D squared from the Contracting Officer memorandum of 26 August 2026.

The constraint register records each governing clause, value and the sheets, comments or bundles it binds.

The review regulation is ER 415-1-11. It gives two durations. Its paragraph g requires the backcheck to be started 30 calendar days before advertising and requires all comments to be resolved before bid opening or proposal evaluation. Its paragraph e, subparagraph (4) allows about 15 calendar days for backchecking of comments. For a package whose corrections are incorporated before advertisement, the 30-day window binds, because the backcheck must precede the advertisement itself. The 15-day period is the backcheck allowance that binds when corrections are issued as an amendment after advertisement, where resolution must precede bid opening.

Production of the BP-3 corrections takes 15 calendar days from the 31 August 2026 start (22 sheets at 4 sheets per calendar day, rounded up to 6 days, plus 3 bundles at 3 days each, with no non-concurrence days) and finishes on 15 September 2026. That is 55 days before the 9 November 2026 advertisement, so the 30-day backcheck window (which opens on 10 October 2026) is comfortably met and the advertisement date does not move. BP-3 is therefore issued as a pre-advertisement reissue of the corrected design, not as an amendment: no change number is assigned, no continuation sheet is submitted, no revision-block entry is made, sheets are resequenced and the two added sheets are numbered A-402 and M-502. The alternative course, advertising on 9 November and amending afterwards, was rejected because it would add revision marks and revision-block overflow charges for no schedule gain and would require a continuation sheet and a change number that the pre-advertisement course avoids.

## 4. BP-2 issue state and Revision (Issue) block overflow (item c)

BP-2 was advertised on 6 July 2026 and its bid opening is 28 September 2026, so the only lawful issue state is an amendment to the solicitation. Two amendments have already been issued, so the next number in numerical order, in the three-cipher form required by FC 1-300-09N paragraph 18-3, is 0003. The amendment is documented on a continuation sheet with the Standard Form 30 coversheet, and the 15-day backcheck period of ER 415-1-11 paragraph e, subparagraph (4) applies: production finishes on 14 September 2026, the backcheck opens on 15 September 2026 and takes 15 calendar days, so it cannot be complete before the 28 September 2026 bid opening. The bid opening therefore moves 1 calendar day(s) to 29 September 2026 and the extension charge is 2,600 x 1 + 140 x 1 = 2,740.00 USD.

The Revision (Issue) block provided by the A/E/C Graphics Standard holds eight rows. 6 of the BP-2 sheets in this issue already carry eight entries: C-101, M-101, M-501, S-101, S-102, S-502. The graphics standard offers two overflow options and requires the chosen option to be used consistently across the whole set. Option 1 (replace the oldest entry, 520 USD per revised full sheet) would cost 6 x 520 = 3,120 USD. Option 2 (spill above the eighth row, 880 USD per revised full sheet that carries three or more drawing blocks, nothing where the spill area is unoccupied) is charged only on M-101 and S-101, which carry three drawing blocks each, and costs 2 x 880 = 1,760 USD; the other 4 full sheets have fewer than three drawing blocks and cost nothing. Option 2 was adopted set-wide and Option 1 was rejected on cost: 3,120 USD against 1,760 USD, a saving of 1,360 USD, with the spill confined to the unoccupied area above the block on the three-block sheets. The option is applied to every revised sheet in the set, not sheet by sheet, and the new entry is placed above the existing entries (row 9 on the full sheets, the next free row on the others).

## 5. Disposition method, void markups and non-concurrence

Every comment in the two EOR markup logs was assessed against the four-part comment convention of ER 1165-2-217 paragraph 5.8.3 and answered with the three-part response of paragraph 5.8.7 (concur or non-concur, how the comment is resolved, and every location affected). Where a markup cannot direct a change it was closed as void with the ground stated, and no sheet was changed for it:

- EOR-2-017 - Author is not listed on the reviewer roster for this review, so the markup is not a review comment and cannot direct a design change.
- EOR-2-019 - The markup annotation carries no creation timestamp, so it cannot be shown to have been made within the review period or authenticated as a review comment; it cannot direct a change.
- EOR-2-021 - The markup is drawn on the superseded 90 percent print of S-102, which predates the sheet renumbering and is not the issue any change is made against.
- EOR-2-033 - Closed in the 60 percent review with a notation that it was elevated for resolution; that closure was never reopened, so the markup cannot direct a further change.
- EOR-3-012 - The markup is drawn on the superseded 60 percent print of T-501, which predates the sheet renumbering and is not the issue any change is made against.
- EOR-3-020 - The markup annotation carries no creation timestamp, so it cannot be shown to have been made within the review period or authenticated as a review comment; it cannot direct a change.
- EOR-3-022 - Author is not listed on the reviewer roster for this review, so the markup is not a review comment and cannot direct a design change.
- EOR-3-036 - Closed in the 60 percent review with a notation that it was elevated for resolution; that closure was never reopened, so the markup cannot direct a further change.

Three yellow text notes reading CHECKED - NO COMMENT (K. Aoyama) are participation notes with no comment record, and the four fire protection comments in the other-discipline log belong to a separate A-E task order; none is an EOR review comment of BP-2 or BP-3, so none is carried into the disposition register. The markup colour convention of ERDC/ITL SR-21-6 distinguishes additions (green), deletions (red) and items requiring clarification (blue); the blue markups are the non-directive preferences. Under ER 1165-2-217 paragraph 5.8.5 a comment that only enforces a personal preference is not directive. Each non-directive comment was priced both ways and the cheaper lawful course taken. EOR-2-011 (bearing area table relocation) is documented as a non-concurrence because adopting it would draw in three civil sheets that are not otherwise in the issue, at 4,347 USD, against 2,400 USD for the documented non-concurrence plus one processing day; the arrangement as drawn is legible and has no code basis for change. The other non-directive markups lie on sheets that this issue already reissues, so they were adopted at the price of the markup extent alone (26 USD per square inch, roughly 170 to 250 USD each), which is far below the 2,400 USD non-concurrence charge and avoids a non-concurrence processing day.

Reference sweep. The reference graph was read from the drawing-block callouts printed in the production data of each sheet. A callout for a detail must point to a 5-series sheet, an enlarged area to a 4-series sheet, a section to a 3-series sheet and an elevation to a 2-series sheet (A/E/C Graphics Standard paragraphs 4.2.4.2 to 4.2.4.4); every callout in both sets was checked against those couplings. Reissue was propagated transitively in the reverse direction: every sheet whose drawing block calls out a changed sheet is reissued, and that in turn draws in the sheets that call out the reissued sheet. The BP-2 change to the equipment anchorage on S-502, for example, reaches E-501, M-501, M-502, S-102 and then M-102, M-301, M-101, M-401 and E-101; the BP-3 change to the structural details on S-501 reaches eighteen sheets across four disciplines.

## 6. Title block findings

Each sheet in the two issues was read against FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-4.1: the CHK initials may not be the same as the DES or DRW initials, and the electronic seal must be that of the discipline responsible for the sheet, consistent with FAR 52.236-25. The non-compliant sheets are:

- BP-2 E-501 - seal is for a different discipline than the sheet content
- BP-3 A-501 - CHECKED BY initials equal DESIGNED BY initials
- BP-3 M-101 - seal is for a different discipline than the sheet content
- BP-3 T-101 - CHECKED BY initials equal DRAWN BY initials

These are corrected on the reissued sheets before signature and seal: the CHK initials are assigned to a checker other than the designer or drafter, and the seal is replaced with the seal of the discipline responsible for the sheet (electrical for E-501 in BP-2, mechanical for M-101 in BP-3). Sheets not in the issue were not reissued and their defects are not charged to this issue, but C-102 in BP-2 carries the same CHK-equals-DES condition and should be corrected at the next reissue.

## 7. Issue content, packaging and cost

**BP-2** - AMENDMENT. 15 sheets in the issue (13 reissued, 2 added), 3 bundles. Ledger: bundles $14,400.00; sheets including markup incorporation $21,576.92; added sheets $12,800.00; revision marks $3,600.00; overflow option $1,760.00; non-concurrence $2,400.00; delay $2,740.00; total $59,276.92 USD.

**BP-3** - PRE_ADVERTISEMENT_REISSUE. 22 sheets in the issue (20 reissued, 2 added), 3 bundles. Ledger: bundles $14,400.00; sheets including markup incorporation $30,033.30; added sheets $12,800.00; revision marks $0.00; overflow option $0.00; non-concurrence $0.00; delay $0.00; total $57,233.30 USD.

Bundling observes the 50 MB drawing-PDF limit of FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-3.5.1. Each bundle is at or below 50 MB and complete discipline sets are kept whole wherever they fit, as paragraph 12-3.5.2.1 requires. In BP-2 the mechanical set alone exceeds 50 MB, so it is the only discipline split, into two parts, and no discipline set is otherwise broken. In BP-3 the architectural set fills one bundle and the structural and mechanical sets share the second; the electrical and telecommunications sets share the third. Every bundle is bookmarked by discipline and by sheet, and the sheets are signed and sealed before delivery per paragraph 12-3.5.2.

Production duration follows the rate schedule note: the whole-day ceiling of sheets produced divided by 4 sheets per day, plus 3 days per bundle, plus 1 day per non-concurrence. The extension charge uses D = max(0, production finish + backcheck window - controlling deadline) and the rate 2,600 x D + 140 x D squared from the Contracting Officer memorandum of 26 August 2026.

The sheets line folds in the markup incorporation charge at 26 USD per square inch (BP-2 166.42 square inches, BP-3 182.05 square inches) because the ledger structure carries no separate markup line; the sheet re-issue charge alone is 1,150 USD per sheet. The combined Government cost of issuing both sets of corrections is 116,510.22 USD, delivered as the one submission this memorandum package accompanies.

Added sheets follow the shipped standards for the issue state. For the advertised BP-2 set the existing sheet numbers are not changed and the two inserted sheets take the supplemental designator of the preceding sheet in their series, M-501A and S-201A, as A/E/C CAD Standard paragraph 2.4.4.1 provides. For the pre-advertisement BP-3 set resequencing is still available, so the two new sheets take the next free sequence numbers in their type series, A-402 (large-scale view) and M-502 (details).

The constraint register records each governing clause, value and the sheets, comments or bundles it binds.

The other non-directive markups were adopted because they cost less than a non-concurrence: most sit on sheets this issue already reissues and cost only the markup extent (26 USD per square inch, roughly 170 to 250 USD each), and the one that draws in a new sheet (EOR-2-013 on E-001) costs 1,728 USD including the reissue and revision mark. ## 6. Title block findings

Each sheet in the two issues was read against FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-4.1: the CHK initials may not be the same as the DES or DRW initials, and the electronic seal must be that of the discipline responsible for the sheet, consistent with FAR 52.236-25. The non-compliant sheets are:

- BP-2 E-501 - seal is for a different discipline than the sheet content
- BP-3 A-501 - CHECKED BY initials equal DESIGNED BY initials
- BP-3 M-101 - seal is for a different discipline than the sheet content
- BP-3 T-101 - CHECKED BY initials equal DRAWN BY initials

These are corrected on the reissued sheets before signature and seal: the CHK initials are assigned to a checker other than the designer or drafter, and the seal is replaced with the seal of the discipline responsible for the sheet (electrical for E-501 in BP-2, mechanical for M-101 in BP-3). ## 1. Documents that govern, and documents set aside

The governing design procedures criteria is FC 1-300-09N, 17 May 2024 with Change 1 of 17 April 2025. Its paragraph 12-3.3.4 fixes the order of precedence for CAD standards: the requirements of its own Chapter 12 come first, then the latest releases of the DoD A/E/C CAD Standard and the A/E/C Graphics Standard, then the National CAD Standard. The current releases in the project file are the A/E/C CAD Standard Release 6.2 (ERDC/ITL SR-24-3) and the A/E/C Graphics Standard Release 2.2 (ERDC/ITL SR-23-1).

Set aside: UFC 1-300-09N (2005, Change 7) is cancelled and is superseded by the FC; the A/E/C CAD Standard Release 6.0 (TR-12-6) is superseded by Release 6.2; the A/E/C Graphics Standard Release 2.1 is superseded by Release 2.2; the GSA PBS CAD Standard 2021 is another agency standard; the fire protection comment log belongs to a separate A-E task order and discipline; and the superseded 90 percent and 60 percent prints are not the issue any change is made against.

The Contracting Officer memorandum of 26 August 2026 adopts ER 1165-2-217 and the markup and record-package conventions of ERDC/ITL SR-21-6 for this work order. ER 415-1-11 governs the timing of the review backcheck. FAR 52.236-25 requires that design work be prepared, reviewed and approved by registered professionals in the particular professional field involved, which is the basis of the seal findings below.

## 2. Revision-graphics layer conflict resolved (item a)

The two shipped documents that disagree are FC 1-300-09N and the A/E/C CAD Standard Release 6.2. FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-3.6.1 places revision clouds on layer Z-ANNO-REVC and revision symbols, notes and revision-block entries on layer Z-ANNO-REVS. The A/E/C CAD Standard Release 6.2 assigns the same two functions to G-ANNO-REVC and G-ANNO-REVS. The clause that fixes the order of precedence is FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-3.3.4: the requirements of its own Chapter 12 rank ahead of the A/E/C CAD Standard and the A/E/C Graphics Standard, which in turn rank ahead of the National CAD Standard. The revision-graphics requirement sits in the FC Chapter 12, so the FC prevails and the layers actually used for every revised sheet in this issue are Z-ANNO-REVC (clouds) and Z-ANNO-REVS (revision triangles, indicators, notes and the Revision (Issue) block entries). The A/E/C CAD Standard G-ANNO-REVC and G-ANNO-REVS layer names were not used. Every revised sheet therefore carries its change clouded on Z-ANNO-REVC with an equilateral triangle numbered 3 beside the cloud, and the Revision (Issue) block entry and note text on Z-ANNO-REVS; the two added sheets carry the same mark 3 with the description SHEET ADDED IN ACCORDANCE WITH AMDT 0003.

## 3. BP-3 issue state (item b)

BP-3 has not been advertised. The solicitation schedule export shows a scheduled advertisement of 12 October 2026, but the later Contracting Officer memorandum of 26 August 2026 states that BP-3 is scheduled to advertise on 9 November 2026; the memorandum is the later dated instrument and controls, so the advertisement date used is 9 November 2026 and the bid opening date remains 12 November 2026.

The review regulation is ER 415-1-11. It gives two durations. Its paragraph g requires the backcheck to be started 30 calendar days before advertising and requires all comments to be resolved before bid opening or proposal evaluation. Its paragraph e, subparagraph (4) allows about 15 calendar days for backchecking of comments. For a package whose corrections are incorporated before advertisement, the 30-day window binds, because the backcheck must precede the advertisement itself. The 15-day period is the backcheck allowance that binds when corrections are issued as an amendment after advertisement, where resolution must precede bid opening.

Production of the BP-3 corrections takes 15 calendar days from the 31 August 2026 start (22 sheets at 4 sheets per calendar day, rounded up to 6 days, plus 3 bundles at 3 days each, with no non-concurrence days) and finishes on 15 September 2026. That is 55 days before the 9 November 2026 advertisement, so the 30-day backcheck window (which opens on 10 October 2026) is comfortably met and the advertisement date does not move. The title block ISSUE DATE on the BP-3 sheets becomes NOVEMBER 2026, the month of advertisement (the BP-2 sheets keep JULY 2026, their advertisement month, and are distinguished by the new revision-block date). BP-3 is therefore issued as a pre-advertisement reissue of the corrected design, not as an amendment: no change number is assigned, no continuation sheet is submitted, no revision-block entry is made, sheets are resequenced and the two added sheets are numbered A-402 and M-502. The alternative course, advertising on 9 November and amending afterwards, was rejected because it would add revision marks and revision-block overflow charges for no schedule gain and would require a continuation sheet and a change number that the pre-advertisement course avoids.

## 4. BP-2 issue state and Revision (Issue) block overflow (item c)

BP-2 was advertised on 6 July 2026 and its bid opening is 28 September 2026, so the only lawful issue state is an amendment to the solicitation. Two amendments have already been issued, so the next number in numerical order, in the three-cipher form required by FC 1-300-09N paragraph 18-3, is 0003. The amendment is documented on a continuation sheet with the Standard Form 30 coversheet, and the 15-day backcheck period of ER 415-1-11 paragraph e, subparagraph (4) applies: production finishes on 14 September 2026, the backcheck opens on 15 September 2026 and takes 15 calendar days, so it cannot be complete before the 28 September 2026 bid opening. The bid opening therefore moves 1 calendar day(s) to 29 September 2026 and the extension charge is 2,600 x 1 + 140 x 1 = 2,740.00 USD.

The Revision (Issue) block provided by the A/E/C Graphics Standard holds eight rows. Six of the BP-2 sheets in this issue already carry eight entries: C-101, M-101, M-501, S-101, S-102, S-502. The graphics standard offers two overflow options and requires the chosen option to be used consistently across the whole set. Option 1 (replace the oldest entry, 520 USD per revised full sheet) would cost 6 x 520 = 3,120 USD. Option 2 (spill above the eighth row, 880 USD per revised full sheet that carries three or more drawing blocks, nothing where the spill area is unoccupied) is charged only on M-101 and S-101, which carry three drawing blocks each, and costs 2 x 880 = 1,760 USD; the other 4 full sheets have fewer than three drawing blocks and cost nothing. Option 2 was adopted set-wide and Option 1 was rejected on cost: 3,120 USD against 1,760 USD, a saving of 1,360 USD, with the spill confined to the unoccupied area above the block on the three-block sheets. The option is applied to every revised sheet in the set, not sheet by sheet, and the new entry is placed above the existing entries (row 9 on the full sheets, the next free row on the others).

## 5. Disposition method, void markups and non-concurrence

Every comment in the two EOR markup logs was assessed against the four-part comment convention of ER 1165-2-217 paragraph 5.8.3 and answered with the three-part response of paragraph 5.8.7 (concur or non-concur, how the comment is resolved, and every location affected). Where a markup cannot direct a change it was closed as void with the ground stated, and no sheet was changed for it:

# Issue the EOR review corrections: Fleet Data Center Increment 2, work order 74213

## Situation

You are the Designer of Record's document controller for work order 74213 at Naval Support
Activity Ventura Bay. Two bid packages are in the pre-award phase and an Engineer-of-Record design
review has just closed on both:

* **BP-2: Central Utility Plant and Site Utilities**, already advertised;
* **BP-3: Data Hall 210 Shell and Interiors**, certified and scheduled to advertise.

The reviewers marked up the drawing sheets and entered their comments in the review record. Your
job is to turn those markups into an issued revision of the drawing package: decide what each
comment does, work out everything each accepted change drags in, regenerate the sheet index,
write the revision-block content, package the re-issued sheets for delivery, and hand the
Contracting Officer the change documentation, at the lowest cost to the Government that the
governing criteria permit.

The project documents are under `project/`: the drawing sheets (`drawings/`: the current issue of
each package, plus earlier submittal prints and record prints from an earlier contract), the review
record (`review/`: the exported markup logs, the review checklists and the reviewer roster), the
governing standards and regulations (`standards/`), the contract documents (`contract/`), the
sheet-index database exports (`index/`), correspondence and rate schedules (`correspondence/`) and
the deliverable schemas (`templates/`). Several documents are reference material only or belong to
another scope; deciding which of them govern is part of the job. Parameters are found in the
documents and are never restated here.

The markups are real annotation objects on the sheets, carrying their author, timestamp, colour and
note. The callout bubbles are drawn on the sheets; nothing in the corpus tabulates them. The review
record carries the submitted parts of each comment only; the evaluation, the response and the
closure are yours to produce.

## Concerns the package must address

**Which markups can drive a change.** Not every markup can. Work out, from the corpus, on what
grounds a markup is unable to direct a design change, and apply those grounds; nothing is tagged.
A markup that cannot direct a change still has to be closed and recorded, with the ground stated.

**What each surviving comment does.** Comments that are directive under the review policy must be
incorporated. Comments that are not directive may be answered with a documented non-concurrence;
that is an engineering and cost judgement, not a formality, and non-concurrence is not free.

**What an accepted change drags in.** A change to a view forces the re-issue of every sheet that
references it, and that sweep is transitive and crosses disciplines. The reference graph is not
given: it is on the sheets.

**The issue state.** For each package decide whether the corrections are incorporated in the design
before the solicitation is advertised or issued as a change to the solicitation afterwards. One
package has only one lawful answer; the other genuinely has two, and they carry different graphics,
different numbering, different documentation and different schedule consequences. Read the dates out
of the contract documents and the applicable window out of the review regulation. The regulation
gives more than one duration; which one binds follows from the issue state you choose. Say which
window you applied and why. Where the BP-3 scheduled advertisement date conflicts between the earlier
schedule export and the later dated Contracting Officer memorandum, the memorandum controls.

**Identification and graphics.** Revision marks, the Revision (Issue) block, sheet identification,
added-sheet designators, the callout-to-sheet-type coupling, the index ordering and the layers that
carry the revision graphics all follow the shipped standards. Two shipped documents appear to
disagree about the revision-graphics layers; the same corpus fixes the order of precedence that
settles it. Do not assume generic drafting practice: where a shipped standard departs from it, the
shipped standard governs, and where two releases of the same standard are in the folder, only one
of them is current.

**Title blocks.** Read the title blocks of the sheets you are re-issuing against the criteria for
signing and sealing and report every sheet that does not comply, with the nature of the defect.

**Packaging and schedule.** The delivered PDFs are capped, discipline sets may not be broken up,
production has a published throughput and each delivered file and each non-concurrence costs
calendar days. Extending the solicitation period costs money and the cost escalates.

## Objective

Minimise the total cost to the Government of issuing the corrections, per the rates published in
the project correspondence: the per-file setup, the per-sheet re-issue charge and the charge on the
extent of markup actually incorporated on each sheet, the added-sheet charge, the revision-mark and
overflow charges where they apply, the non-concurrence charge, and the solicitation-period
extension. Your plan is scored against a certified relaxation bound on the same problem, so the
bound is not attainable; a competent plan scores close to it.

If production moves the controlling advertisement or bid-opening deadline by `D` calendar days,
the extension charge is exactly `2,600 × D + 140 × D²` USD, with `D = max(0, finish − deadline)`.

**Licensing rule (hard):** do not reproduce the text of any shipped standard or regulation in your
narrative deliverables. Cite the document, the clause and the value, and say what the clause
requires in your own words. The check fails on a verbatim run of **16 or more consecutive words**
taken from a shipped standard's provision text; a word is a run of two or more letters, so numbers,
single letters and punctuation are not counted. Clause and paragraph headings, figure and table
captions and document titles are **not** provision text and are never counted (you may name a
clause by its heading), and neither are the few sentences the design basis is expressly required to
state. **Citation rule (hard):** every clause number you cite must be one the shipped documents
actually contain. The check looks only at numbers presented as **authority**: a number introduced
by a section sign, by a clause word (section, clause, paragraph, table, figure, appendix, chapter,
article, item) or by a document's name. Ordinary numbers in your prose (sizes, areas, costs,
percentages, day counts, sheet counts) are never read as clause numbers.

## Deliverable

A single file `output/submission.zip` (at most 25 MB and 200 files) containing exactly these seven
files, at the top level, covering **both** packages:

1. `disposition_register.csv`: one row per EOR review comment, columns per
   `templates/disposition_register.schema.json`.
2. `sheet_index.csv`: the regenerated index of each package in the order the governing standard
   sets, columns per `templates/sheet_index.schema.json`.
3. `revision_log.csv`: the Revision (Issue) block content for every sheet in the issue, columns
   per `templates/revision_log.schema.json`. Where a package's issue state means no revision entry
   is made, say so in the row rather than omitting the sheet.
4. `issue_plan.csv`: the delivered bundling, columns per `templates/issue_plan.schema.json`.
5. `continuation_sheet.md`: the change documentation for the Contracting Officer, in the format
   the criteria document's sample lays down, including the drawing-list document it names. A
   package whose corrections are not issued as a change to a solicitation gets a short statement
   saying so instead.
6. `constraint_register.xlsx`: the register of every requirement you applied
   (`templates/constraint_register_template.xlsx` columns): the real document, the clause, the
   value and the items it binds. **The register is scored**: a family whose governing clause you
   did not register earns no credit even if your answer is right. Rows that should not have been
   filed (a superseded release, a cancelled document, another agency's or another discipline's
   document, or a clause the cited document does not contain) reduce the register's precision;
   extra *correct* rows are neutral. **The first 400 rows are scanned, and the precision floor is
   0.60**: below that floor the constraint term is scaled down proportionally.
7. `design_basis.md`: the design basis. It must embed exactly one fenced ```json block:

```
{"packages": {"BP-2": {"issue_state": "AMENDMENT" | "PRE_ADVERTISEMENT_REISSUE",
                       "change_number": "<as the criteria document forms it, or \"\">",
                       "overflow_option": 1 | 2 | "NONE",
                       "revision_layers": ["<layer>", ...],
                       "n_bundles": N, "production_days": N, "delay_days": N,
                       "backcheck_window_days": N,
                       "ledger": {"bundles_usd": N, "sheets_usd": N, "added_sheets_usd": N,
                                  "revision_marks_usd": N, "overflow_option_usd": N,
                                  "non_concurrence_usd": N, "delay_usd": N, "total_usd": N},
                       "title_block_defects": [{"sheet": "<id>", "defect": "CHK_EQUALS_DES" |
                                                "CHK_EQUALS_DRW" | "SEAL_DISCIPLINE_MISMATCH"}]},
              "BP-3": { ... same shape ... }},
 "governing_standards": ["<title and release/edition>", ...],
 "rejected_standards": ["<title and release/edition> - <why it does not govern>", ...],
 "rate_parameters": {"production_start": "YYYY-MM-DD", "sheets_per_day": N, "days_per_bundle": N},
 "void_markups": [{"comment_id": "<id>", "reason": "<the ground, in your own words>"}]}
```

followed by a narrative that (a) resolves the revision-graphics layer conflict between the two
shipped standards, naming the clause that fixes the order of precedence and the layers actually
used; (b) decides BP-3's issue state from the advertisement and bid-opening dates and the review
regulation's window, stating the number of calendar days in the window applied and why that window
rather than the other; and (c) explains the Revision (Issue) block overflow decision for BP-2:
the row capacity, which option was taken, that the option is applied set-wide rather than sheet by
sheet, and the cost reason the other option was rejected. These three statements are judged against
quoted evidence: a claim with nothing quotable behind it scores nothing.

## Grading

Graded items are the EOR review comments of both bid packages. Each package is assessed in the
issue state you declare for it, against its own recomputed plan cost. Requirement families are
tagged HARD or SOFT. The HARD families cover the principal decisions on each comment, the
package-level requirements of the governing documents, the licensing and citation rules, and the
design basis's listing of every markup that cannot direct a change, with its ground. The SOFT
families cover the remaining documentation and presentation requirements, two further design-basis
program items and the three judged narrative items. A family earns credit only if it is both
satisfied and registered in your constraint register. There are 30 families, 17 of them HARD.
Per comment the score is 0.4 × p + 0.6 × [h = 1] × O′, where p is the fraction of the 30 families
satisfied-and-registered (scaled down below the precision floor as stated above), h the fraction
of the 17 HARD families satisfied-and-registered ([h = 1] is 1 when all 17 are, else 0), O the
objective credit (certified relaxation bound / your plan's recomputed cost, at most 1), and
O′ = clip((O − O_naive) / (1 − O_naive), 0, 1), where O_naive is the credit of a naive baseline plan
for the comment's package. A HARD miss removes the objective credit from the row. A missing or
unparseable row scores 0. The task score is
the mean over the graded comments.

Your plan's cost is recomputed by the grader from what your submission actually contains, at the
published rates; understating a line in the ledger does not make a plan cheaper, it fails the
ledger family.

**Every threshold the grader applies, in full; nothing else is hidden.** The register precision
floor is 0.60 and only the first 400 register rows are scanned. `output/submission.zip` is at most
25 MB, 200 files and 100 MB uncompressed. The licensing check's verbatim run is 16 words, as above.
A documented non-concurrence needs a written resolution of at least six words, and a void markup a
stated ground of at least four. Each line of the cost ledger must recompute to within the greater
of 0.5 % and $1. Everything else the grader checks is a value or a rule that lives in the shipped
documents.


## Verifier access (blind variant)

No verifier, oracle, or evaluation data of any kind is available in this workspace; the
only checks you can run are the ones you build yourself. Work from the brief and the
documents alone and submit your best final deliverable; it will be graded offline by the
frozen verifier.
