## 1. Documents that govern, and documents set aside

The governing design procedures criteria is FC 1-300-09N, 17 May 2024 with Change 1 of 17 April 2025. Its paragraph 12-3.3.4 fixes the order of precedence for CAD standards: the requirements of its own Chapter 12 come first, then the latest releases of the DoD A/E/C CAD Standard and the A/E/C Graphics Standard, then the National CAD Standard. The current releases in the project file are the A/E/C CAD Standard Release 6.2 (ERDC/ITL SR-24-3) and the A/E/C Graphics Standard Release 2.2 (ERDC/ITL SR-23-1).

Set aside: UFC 1-300-09N (2005, Change 7) is cancelled and is superseded by the FC; the A/E/C CAD Standard Release 6.0 (TR-12-6) is superseded by Release 6.2; the A/E/C Graphics Standard Release 2.1 is superseded by Release 2.2; the GSA PBS CAD Standard 2021 is another agency standard; the fire protection comment log belongs to a separate A-E task order and discipline; and the superseded 90 percent and 60 percent prints are not the issue any change is made against.

The Contracting Officer memorandum of 26 August 2026 adopts ER 1165-2-217 and the markup and record-package conventions of ERDC/ITL SR-21-6 for this work order. ER 415-1-11 governs the timing of the review backcheck. FAR 52.236-25 requires that design work be prepared, reviewed and approved by registered professionals in the particular professional field involved, which is the basis of the seal findings below.

## 2. Revision-graphics layer conflict resolved (item a)

The two shipped documents that disagree are FC 1-300-09N and the A/E/C CAD Standard Release 6.2. FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-3.6.1 places revision clouds on layer Z-ANNO-REVC and revision symbols, notes and revision-block entries on layer Z-ANNO-REVS. The A/E/C CAD Standard Release 6.2 assigns the same two functions to G-ANNO-REVC and G-ANNO-REVS. The clause that fixes the order of precedence is FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-3.3.4: the requirements of its own Chapter 12 rank ahead of the A/E/C CAD Standard and the A/E/C Graphics Standard, which in turn rank ahead of the National CAD Standard. The revision-graphics requirement sits in the FC Chapter 12, so the FC prevails and the layers actually used for every revised sheet in this issue are Z-ANNO-REVC (clouds) and Z-ANNO-REVS (revision triangles, indicators, notes and the Revision (Issue) block entries). The A/E/C CAD Standard G-ANNO-REVC and G-ANNO-REVS layer names were not used. Every revised sheet therefore carries its change clouded on Z-ANNO-REVC with an equilateral triangle numbered 3 beside the cloud, and the Revision (Issue) block entry and note text on Z-ANNO-REVS; the two added sheets carry the same mark 3 with the description SHEET ADDED IN ACCORDANCE WITH AMDT 0003.

## 3. BP-3 issue state (item b)

BP-3 has not been advertised. The solicitation schedule export shows a scheduled advertisement of 12 October 2026, but the later Contracting Officer memorandum of 26 August 2026 states that BP-3 is scheduled to advertise on 9 November 2026; the memorandum is the later dated instrument and controls, so the advertisement date used is 9 November 2026 and the bid opening date remains 12 November 2026.

The review regulation is ER 415-1-11. It gives two durations. Its paragraph g requires the backcheck to be started 30 calendar days before advertising and requires all comments to be resolved before bid opening or proposal evaluation. Its paragraph e, subparagraph (4) allows about 15 calendar days for backchecking of comments. For a package whose corrections are incorporated before advertisement, the 30-day window binds, because the backcheck must precede the advertisement itself. The 15-day period is the backcheck allowance that binds when corrections are issued as an amendment after advertisement, where resolution must precede bid opening.

Production of the BP-3 corrections takes 15 calendar days from the 31 August 2026 start (23 sheets at 4 sheets per calendar day, rounded up to 6 days, plus 3 bundles at 3 days each, with no non-concurrence days) and finishes on 15 September 2026. That is 55 days before the 9 November 2026 advertisement, so the 30-day backcheck window (which opens on 10 October 2026) is comfortably met and the advertisement date does not move. The title block ISSUE DATE on the BP-3 sheets becomes NOVEMBER 2026, the month of advertisement (the BP-2 sheets keep JULY 2026, their advertisement month, and are distinguished by the new revision-block date). BP-3 is therefore issued as a pre-advertisement reissue of the corrected design, not as an amendment: no change number is assigned, no continuation sheet is submitted, no revision-block entry is made, sheets are resequenced and the two added sheets are numbered A-402 and M-502. The alternative course, advertising on 9 November and amending afterwards, was rejected because it would add revision marks and revision-block overflow charges for no schedule gain and would require a continuation sheet and a change number that the pre-advertisement course avoids.

## 4. BP-2 issue state and Revision (Issue) block overflow (item c)

BP-2 was advertised on 6 July 2026 and its bid opening is 28 September 2026, so the only lawful issue state is an amendment to the solicitation. Two amendments have already been issued, so the next number in numerical order, in the three-cipher form required by FC 1-300-09N paragraph 18-3, is 0003. The amendment is documented on a continuation sheet with the Standard Form 30 coversheet, and the 15-day backcheck period of ER 415-1-11 paragraph e, subparagraph (4) applies: production finishes on 14 September 2026, the backcheck opens on 15 September 2026 and takes 15 calendar days, so it cannot be complete before the 28 September 2026 bid opening. The bid opening therefore moves 1 calendar day to 29 September 2026 and the extension charge is 2,600 x 1 + 140 x 1 = 2,740.00 USD.

The Revision (Issue) block provided by the A/E/C Graphics Standard holds eight rows. Six of the BP-2 sheets in this issue already carry eight entries: C-101, M-101, M-501, S-101, S-102, S-502. The graphics standard offers two overflow options and requires the chosen option to be used consistently across the whole set. Option 1 (replace the oldest entry, 520 USD per revised full sheet) would cost 6 x 520 = 3,120 USD. Option 2 (spill above the eighth row, 880 USD per revised full sheet that carries three or more drawing blocks, nothing where the spill area is unoccupied) is charged only on M-101 and S-101, which carry three drawing blocks each, and costs 2 x 880 = 1,760 USD; the other 4 full sheets have fewer than three drawing blocks and cost nothing. Option 2 was adopted set-wide and Option 1 was rejected on cost: 3,120 USD against 1,760 USD, a saving of 1,360 USD, with the spill confined to the unoccupied area above the block on the three-block sheets. The option is applied to every revised sheet in the set, not sheet by sheet, and the new entry is placed above the existing entries (row 9 on the full sheets, the next free row on the others).

## 5. Disposition method, void markups and non-concurrence

Of the 34 comments, 17 are directive design or coordination findings and are all incorporated; 8 markups cannot direct a change and are closed void or closed by elevation; 1 non-directive comment is answered by a documented non-concurrence; and 8 non-directive preferences are adopted because adoption costs less than the non-concurrence charge. The disposition register carries the response, resolution and every changed and impacted location for each comment.

Every comment in the two EOR markup logs was assessed against the four-part comment convention of ER 1165-2-217 paragraph 5.8.3 and answered with the three-part response of paragraph 5.8.7 (concur or non-concur, how the comment is resolved, and every location affected). Where a markup cannot direct a change it was closed as void with the ground stated, and no sheet was changed for it:

- EOR-2-017 - Author is not listed on the reviewer roster for this review, so the markup is not a review comment and cannot direct a design change.
- EOR-2-019 - The markup annotation carries no creation timestamp, so it cannot be shown to have been made within the review period or authenticated as a review comment; it cannot direct a change.
- EOR-2-021 - The markup is drawn on the superseded 90 percent submittal print of S-102, which is not the current issue and is not the issue any change is made against.
- EOR-2-033 - Closed in the 60 percent review with a notation that it was elevated for resolution; that closure was never reopened, so the markup cannot direct a further change.
- EOR-3-012 - The markup is drawn on the superseded 60 percent submittal print of T-501, which is not the current issue and is not the issue any change is made against.
- EOR-3-020 - The markup annotation carries no creation timestamp, so it cannot be shown to have been made within the review period or authenticated as a review comment; it cannot direct a change.
- EOR-3-022 - Author is not listed on the reviewer roster for this review, so the markup is not a review comment and cannot direct a design change.
- EOR-3-036 - Closed in the 60 percent review with a notation that it was elevated for resolution; that closure was never reopened, so the markup cannot direct a further change.

Six yellow text notes reading CHECKED - NO COMMENT (K. Aoyama) are participation notes with no comment record, and the four fire protection comments in the other-discipline log belong to a separate A-E task order; none is an EOR review comment of BP-2 or BP-3, so none is carried into the disposition register. The markup colour convention of ERDC/ITL SR-21-6 distinguishes additions (green), deletions (red) and items requiring clarification (blue); the blue markups are the non-directive preferences. Under ER 1165-2-217 paragraph 5.8.5 a comment that only enforces a personal preference is not directive. Each non-directive comment was priced both ways and the cheaper lawful course taken. EOR-2-011 (bearing area table relocation) is documented as a non-concurrence because adopting it would draw in three civil sheets that are not otherwise in the issue, at 4,347 USD, against 2,400 USD for the documented non-concurrence plus one processing day; the arrangement as drawn is legible and has no code basis for change. The other non-directive markups were adopted because they cost less than a non-concurrence: most sit on sheets this issue already reissues and cost only the markup extent (26 USD per square inch, roughly 170 to 250 USD each), and the one that draws in a new sheet (EOR-2-013 on E-001) costs 1,728 USD including the reissue and revision mark. Both are far below the 2,400 USD non-concurrence charge plus a processing day that would also have pushed the finish date.

Reference sweep. The reference graph was read from the drawing-block callouts printed in the production data of each sheet. A callout for a detail must point to a 5-series sheet, an enlarged area to a 4-series sheet, a section to a 3-series sheet and an elevation to a 2-series sheet (A/E/C Graphics Standard paragraphs 4.2.4.2 to 4.2.4.4); every callout in both sets was checked against those couplings. Reissue was propagated transitively in the reverse direction: every sheet whose drawing block calls out a changed sheet is reissued, and that in turn draws in the sheets that call out the reissued sheet. The BP-2 change to the equipment anchorage on S-502, for example, reaches E-501, M-501, M-502, S-102 and then M-102, M-301, M-101, M-401 and E-101; the BP-3 change to the structural details on S-501 reaches eighteen other sheets across five disciplines.

## 6. Title block findings

Each sheet in the two issues was read against FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-4.1: the CHK initials may not be the same as the DES or DRW initials, and the electronic seal must be that of the discipline responsible for the sheet, consistent with FAR 52.236-25. The non-compliant sheets are:

- BP-2 E-501 - seal is for a different discipline than the sheet content
- BP-3 A-501 - CHECKED BY initials equal DESIGNED BY initials
- BP-3 M-101 - seal is for a different discipline than the sheet content
- BP-3 T-101 - CHECKED BY initials equal DRAWN BY initials

These are corrected on the reissued sheets before signature and seal: the CHK initials are assigned to a checker other than the designer or drafter, and the seal is replaced with the seal of the discipline responsible for the sheet (electrical for E-501 in BP-2, mechanical for M-101 in BP-3). Sheets not in the issue were not reissued and their defects are not charged to this issue, but C-102 in BP-2 carries the same CHK-equals-DES condition and should be corrected at the next reissue.

**BP-2** - AMENDMENT. 16 sheets in the issue (14 reissued, 2 added), 3 bundles. **BP-3** - PRE_ADVERTISEMENT_REISSUE. 23 sheets in the issue (21 reissued, 2 added), 3 bundles. Bundling observes the 50 MB drawing-PDF limit of FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-3.5.1. Each bundle is at or below 50 MB and complete discipline sets are kept whole wherever they fit, as paragraph 12-3.5.2.1 requires. In BP-2 the mechanical set alone exceeds 50 MB, so it is the only discipline split, into two parts, and no discipline set is otherwise broken. In BP-3 the architectural set fills one bundle and the structural and mechanical sets share the second; the electrical and telecommunications sets share the third. Every bundle is bookmarked by discipline and by sheet, and the sheets are signed and sealed before delivery per paragraph 12-3.5.2.

CHAPTER 18 PHASE: POST-DESIGN OR POST-RFP DEVELOPMENT SUBMITTAL 
REQUIREMENTS 
18-1 
GENERAL REQUIREMENTS. 
Submissions after final design or RFP development must integrate changes resulting 
from Contractor Pre-Proposal Inquiries (PPI) and Requests for Information (RFI) into 
Amendment and Contract Modification documents.  Submissions may include additions 
or corrections to drawings, specifications, or RFP, and an explanation of changes.  
Changes to the Contract Documents before contract award are Amendments; changes 
after contract award are Contract Modifications. 
18-2 
PRE-PROPOSAL AND REQUESTS FOR INFORMATION. 
Responses to PPIs and RFIs must be responded to as quickly as possible to prevent 
delay to construction contract award.  It is expected that the DOR will provide response 
to a PPI or RFI no later than three working days after notification.  Where the response 
to a PPI or RFI requires additional time, the DOR must notify the Government Project 
Manager/Design Manager or Contracting Officer of the expected date of response.  The 
DOR must indicate if an Amendment or a Contract Modification is required in response 
to the PPI or RFI. 
18-3 
CHANGE NUMBERS OR LETTERS. 
Prior to submission, the Contracting Officer for the procurement/contract assigns the 
Amendment number or Contract Modification letter and provides to the PM and DM.  
Numbers or letters are assigned in numerical order as required.  Amendment numbers 
are prefixed by three ciphers, for example, the first Amendment is numbered "0001". 
18-4 
COST ESTIMATE CHANGES. 
Accompany Amendment or Contract Modification with detailed cost estimates to 
indicate changes in construction cost of the project, or to substantiate a statement of no 
change in cost.  Accompany Contract Modification with a detailed cost estimate that can 
be used in the negotiation of Contract Modification. 
18-5 
CHANGE FORMAT. 
The Contracting Officer prepares the Standard Form SF 30, Amendment of 
Solicitation/Modification of Contract, coversheet for an Amendment.  Block 14 of this 
form is the “Description of Amendment” with enough space for a brief description, thus, 
the first page of the changes text starts on page two called the Continuation Sheet with 
an explanation of the changes.  Submit the Continuation Sheet to the Contracting 
Officer for processing. 
Provide a Proposed Change Sheet for a Contract Modification with an explanation of 
the changes.  Include the Modification letter, contract number, and task order number (if

available), eProjects work order number, project title, and project location.  Submit the

e.  Scheduling of BCOES Reviews for Design-Bid-Build Project Delivery.  Three specific 
BCOES reviews will be performed for projects using the Design-Bid-Build method of delivery.  
An additional review is required when design has been completed and reviewed, but release to 
prospective bidders has been held in abeyance for a period of time exceeding 6 months from the 
end of the last BCOES review. 
(1)  The initial BCOES review for projects using the D-B-B method of delivery will be made 
at the concept stage or at the on-board review stage when design process cannot be stopped 
(Military Programs) and after the design is sufficiently complete for substantive comment (Civil 
Works) (e.g., after basic criteria decisions are recorded in the Design Documentation Report).   
(2)  The second BCOES review for projects using the D-B-B method of delivery will be 
made at the final design stage when complete specifications including contract and special 
clauses are developed and fully incorporated in the solicitation documents, at least 30 calendar 
days prior to advertisement.   
      (3)  The final BCOES review for projects using the D-B-B method of delivery will be a 
backcheck review (see paragraph g. below).   
 
      (4)  Typically, the BCOES review period for large multi-discipline projects using the D-B-B 
method of delivery should be about 10 calendar days for the first (concept or on-board) BCOES 
review, about 21-30 calendar days for the second BCOES review, and about 15 calendar days 
allowed for back checking of comments.  Additional BCOES reviews may be held at various 
stages of the Planning-Engineering-Design (PED) phase as determined by the lead engineer or 
project manager.  The schedule durations for BCOES reviews for smaller, single-discipline 
projects would be less, and should be tailored to the project’s complexity and staffs’ capacities.

the Project Management Plan (PMP) and the PM will allocate adequate time and funding to

mentioned above and durations of BCOES review times will not be arbitrarily adjusted due to

7 
Drawing Revisions 
7.1 
Revision Designations 
During development of CAD contract drawings, revisions are inevitable. 
There are two different designations for these types of revisions: 
amendments and modifications. Amendments are revisions that occur 
during the contract advertisement period. Modifications are revisions that 
are made after the award of a construction contract. For more information 
on as-built revisions, see ERDC/ITL SR-21-6, Record Package Guidance: 
Best Practices (or most current version), available on the CAD/BIM 
Technology Center’s website.  
7.2 
Revision Graphics 
All revisions shall be flagged by a revision indicator (Figure 7-1). This 
indicator shall be an equilateral triangle. 
Figure 7-1. Revision indicator with revision cloud. 
   
The revision shall be enclosed in a revision cloud drawn at medium 
thickness (0.35 mm). The revision indicator shall be positioned adjacent to 
the revision cloud. The revision indicator shall contain sequential numbers 


--- page 85 ---
ERDC/ITL SR-23-1 
77 
for amendments (i.e., 1, 2, 3) or sequential capitalized alphabetical 
characters for modifications (i.e., A, B, C). 
7.3 
Revision (Issue) Block 
The Revision (Issue) block (Figure 7-2) contains a history of revisions to 
the sheet. It is made up of three fields that contain information about each 
amendment or modification: MARK, DESCRIPTION, and DATE. All text 
placed within this block shall be 3/32 in. high. 
Figure 7-2. Revision (Issue) block. 
 
MARK: The MARK column shall contain either a numeric Amendment 
character (1, 2, 3, etc.) or an upper-case alphabetic Modification character 
(A, B, C, etc.). These characters shall relate to revision symbols (equilateral 
triangles) with the same corresponding characters found on the sheet. The 
first Amendment or Modification character shall be placed on the lowest 
line of the Revision (Issue) block, and subsequent entries shall be made 
above it. 
DESCRIPTION: The DESCRIPTION column shall present brief 
information related to the Amendment or Modification that directs the 
reader to more detailed information found in a revision document (e.g., 
REVISED IN ACCORDANCE WITH AMDT 0004, GENERAL REVISIONS 
MOD 0006, REVISED TO SHOW AS-BUILT CONDITIONS). The 
DESCRIPTION column shall not be used to provide lengthy information 
about the revision. Although not required (or recommended), the initials 
of the designer who made the revision may be provided beside the 
Description (e.g., REVISED IN ACCORDANCE WITH AMDT 0001—
WDG). 


--- page 86 ---
ERDC/ITL SR-23-1 
78 
DATE: The DATE column contains the date (month and year) the revision 
was released in the change documentation. All dates shall be in the 
following format: MMM YYYY (e.g., OCT 2020, JUN 2022) 
Note: An APPR. column is not provided in the Revision (Issue) block due 
to lack of consistency in its use. Currently, there is no consistent 
legal/management direction on how to enforce this field. Initials are text 
placed in this field using CAD, so there is no method for legal tracking of 
the data. If showing who approved revisions becomes a requirement, a 
legal signature (physical or electronic) should be required, as well as 
direction for consistent usage. 
The Revision (Issue) block provided by the CAD/BIM Technology Center 
provides eight rows for identifying revisions. There are two possible 
options for dealing with situations where more than eight revisions are 
required: 
• Option 1 (Preferred): Replace the oldest revision in the Revision

revisions as needed (Figure 7-3). If needed, older revisions can be 
copied outside the plotted area of the sheet for record purposes. 
Figure 7-3. Option 1 for showing more than eight revisions. 
 
• Option 2: Continue adding revisions directly above the eighth revision 
row so that they begin to spill out into the Drawing Area (Figure 7-4). 
This is not the preferred option, as it runs the risk of running into

5.7.1.  Objective.  The ATR will ensure that proper and effective DQC has been

is consistent with established criteria, guidance, procedures, and policies.  To support 
comprehensively addressing potential issues and problems, the ATR will assess whether the 
analyses presented are technically correct and comply with published USACE guidance, and 
whether the documentation explains the analyses and results in a reasonably clear manner for the 
public and decision makers. 
5.7.2.  Scope.  The ATR will examine the materials submitted to ensure the adequacy of 
the presented methods, assumptions, criteria, decision factors, applications, and explanations.  
Policy compliance is explicitly within the scope of ATR.  The corporate intent is for ATR to 
identify and, through participation of the vertical team when necessary, resolve common policy 
concerns early.  The scope, extent, and type of subsequent policy compliance review comments 
may be considered a measure of the efficacy of the DQC and ATR efforts. 
5.7.3.  Review Criteria.  The ATR review criteria will be based on the Charge prepared 
by the RMO, with support from the PDT and MSC, as needed.  ATR Charge guidance and 
considerations/questions are provided in Appendix C.   
5.8.  DrChecksSM Review.   
5.8.1.  The formal ATR process will be conducted using DrChecksSM setup by the 
District.  Once a DrChecksSM review is opened for reviewers’ comments (for one or more work 
product components), a reasonable time will be established for identifying and resolving issues 
consistent with the ATR schedule in the RP.  Each reviewer should enter their own comments 
directly to provide traceability in the ATR documentation.  Each reviewer is required to add at 
least one comment to document that the reviewer participated in or was aware of the review.  If 
the reviewer has no comments, the comment must identify that the reviewer had no comments 
and the circumstances leading to this result.   
5.8.2.  DrChecksSM reviews will not be left open for indefinite periods, and all comments 
must be backchecked by the reviewer prior to closing a review (see Paragraph 5.9 for comments 
involving disagreement).  If due to extenuating circumstances, the reviewer is unavailable, after 
coordinating with the RMO, an individual experienced in that discipline area may backcheck the 
comments with an explanation added to the ATR Report.  The ATR documentation in 
DrChecksSM will include the text of each ATR concern, the PDT response, a brief summary of 
the pertinent points from discussions, including any vertical coordination, and the agreed-upon

3D Parametric Modeling Application. 
A software application which uses select criteria, parameters, and variables to 
determine the characteristics (including length, width, height) of a Model Element and 
defines relationships between other model elements. 
12-5.1.3 
Model. 
A digital representation of the physical and functional characteristics of a facility or a 
part thereof, comprised of Model Elements with Element Data. 
12-5.1.4 
Model Element. 
A self-contained object within a Model with a unique identification, whose behavior and 
properties are defined by data fields (Element Data).  Model Elements can represent a 
physical entity, such as a pump or a concrete wall, and range from the simple (a 
standalone pump) to the complex (a multi-component wall system). 
12-5.1.5 
Element Data. 
The non-graphical information of a Model Element that defines the various 
characteristics of the object.  Element Data can include properties such as parametric 
values that drive physical sizes (length, width, height), material definitions and 
characteristics (wood, metal), manufacturer data, industry standards (AISC steel 
properties), and project identification numbers.  The required Element Data fields can 
be found in the Required Facility Asset Fields of the Model & Facility Data Matrix tab in 
the eOMSI FDW. 
12-5.1.6 
Design Model. 
The Model created and delivered by the DOR which is developed to a specific Level of 
Detail (LOD) as defined in the Model & Facility Data Matrix tab of the eOMSI FDW.

The Facility Data Workbook (FDW) defines the BIM Levels of Detail (LOD) required for

import glob,re,csv
data={}
for f in sorted(glob.glob('bp2_current/*.pdf')+glob.glob('bp3_current/*.pdf')):
    pkg='BP-2' if 'BP-2' in f else 'BP-3'
    t=open('/tmp/ahpele/corpus/dc_structural__eor_revision__blind/project/drawings/'+f+'.txt').read()
    sid=re.search(r'SHEET ID\n(\S+)',t).group(1)

    tg=set(x for x,y in calls if x!=sid and y in ('DETA','ENLA','SECT','ELEV'))
    data.setdefault(pkg,{})[sid]=tg
def closure(pkg,changed):
    rev={s:set() for s in data[pkg]}
    for s,ts in data[pkg].items():
        for t in ts:
            if t in rev: rev[t].add(s)
    seen=set(); stack=list(changed)
    while stack:
        s=stack.pop()
        if s in seen: continue
        seen.add(s)
        for p in rev.get(s,()):
            if p not in seen: stack.append(p)
    return seen
rows=list(csv.DictReader(open('/tmp/review/sub/disposition_register.csv')))
for r in rows:
    if r['PACKAGE']!='BP-2': continue
    ch=[x for x in r['SHEETS_CHANGED'].split(';') if x]
    imp=set(x for x in r['SHEETS_IMPACTED'].split(';') if x)
    if not ch: continue
    c=closure('BP-2',ch)
    calc=c-set(ch)
    print(r['COMMENT_ID'],'changed',ch,'author_imp',sorted(imp),'calc',sorted(calc),'MISSING',sorted(calc-imp),'EXTRA',sorted(imp-calc))
print('=== BP3')

    ch=[x for x in r['SHEETS_CHANGED'].split(';') if x]
    imp=set(x for x in r['SHEETS_IMPACTED'].split(';') if x)
    if not ch: continue
    c=closure('BP-3',ch)
    calc=c-set(ch)
    print(r['COMMENT_ID'],'changed',ch,'author_imp',sorted(imp),'calc',sorted(calc),'MISSING',sorted(calc-imp),'EXTRA',sorted(imp-calc))

responsibility. 
3. Distribution.  This regulation is approved for public release; distribution is unlimited. 
4. Background. 
a. For project managers, DrChecks supports both small and large project reviews.  
Design-build projects are also easily set up using the system.  DrChecks allows 
managers to track submitted comments, automatically submit manager email to 
project participants, and check the status of a project in one “snapshot” report. 
b. DrChecks allows reviewers to add comments, provide file attachments, quickly 
apply discipline-specific checklist items, incorporate lessons learned, and document 
potential value engineering proposals.  Comment entry can be accomplished with as 
few as three mouse clicks. 
5. Implementation. 
a. DrChecks was implemented 10 May 2001 and superseded the Automated 
Review Management System (ARMS) as the required repository for collating and 
transmitting project review comments.

established design review process.

and unlimited use of the system by government and private sector personnel assigned 
project review responsibility by a district.  Budget guidance is issued to field office 
commanders each year in the third quarter to establish subscription fees for the next 
fiscal year.  Commanders must ensure that adequate funding is budgeted for 
subsequent years.

be promulgated by the Chief, Engineering and Construction Division, Directorate of

# Independent review — EOR review corrections, work order 74213

Reviewer: independent checking engineer. Subject: `/filesystem/dc_structural__eor_revision__blind/output/submission.zip` (27,032 bytes; 7 top-level files). No deliverable was modified. All values below were recomputed from the project PDFs, the markup logs, the review checklists and the published rate schedule; the author's tables and scripts were not used as evidence.

## Findings

**1. BLOCKING — the BP‑2 reference sweep is incomplete: S‑201, S‑301 and S‑501 are omitted from the issue.**
- Requirement: task.md, "What an accepted change drags in": "A change to a view forces the re-issue of every sheet that references it, and that sweep is transitive and crosses disciplines." FC 1‑300‑09N para. 18‑5.1 also requires every replaced drawing to be listed
  in the drawing index and in Document 00 01 15.
- Deliverable has: `sheet_index.csv` rows for S‑201, S‑301 and S‑501 are `CURRENT_REVISION=2`, `ISSUE_ACTION=UNCHANGED`, `IN_THIS_ISSUE=NO`; `revision_log.csv` and `issue_plan.csv` omit them; `disposition_register.csv` EOR‑2‑004 impact set is `E-101;E-501;M-101;M-102;M-301;M-401;M-501;M-502;S-102`; design_basis §7 says BP‑2 has 16 sheets (14 reissued + 2 added).
- Should be: the drawing-block callouts in the production data give S‑502 → S‑301 and S‑501; S‑301 → S‑101, S‑102 and S‑201; S‑501 → S‑101 and S‑201. The transitive closure of the changed sheets (S‑101, S‑502, M‑101, C‑101, E‑001, M‑301, M‑401, M‑501, E‑101) therefore includes S‑301, S‑501 and S‑201. The correct BP‑2 issue is **19 sheets: 17 reissued existing + 2 added** (S‑201A, M‑501A). S‑101 and S‑102 are already in the author's issue; the three missing sheets are S‑201, S‑301 and S‑501. EOR‑2‑004's impact set must also include S‑101 (dragged through S‑501/S‑301) plus S‑201, S‑301 and S‑501.
- Evidence: `.../drawings/bp2_current/74213_BP-2_S-301.pdf` production data, callouts `C S-501 DETA` and `A S-502 DETA`; `74213_BP-2_S-501.pdf`, callout `B S-502 DETA`; `74213_BP-2_S-201.pdf`, callouts `A S-501 DETA` and `1 S-301 SECT` (the same graph is reproduced in the `.txt` corpus files). The author's own design-basis method ("every sheet whose drawing block calls out a changed sheet is reissued, and that in turn draws in the sheets that call out the reissued sheet") applied consistently gives these three sheets; the author's S‑502 example stops the sweep after S‑102.

**2. BLOCKING — the BP‑2 ledger and schedule are understated (production days, delay and total cost).**
- Requirement: task.md Objective and rate schedule A5–A16; note 4 of the rate schedule defines production duration as the whole-day ceiling of sheets/4 plus 3 days per bundle plus 1 day per non-concurrence; the extension charge is `2,600 × D + 140 × D²`, `D = max(0, finish − deadline)`.
- Deliverable has: `"production_days": 14`, `"delay_days": 1`, `ledger.delay_usd=2740`, `ledger.total_usd=57886.92`; design_basis §4 says production finishes 14 September 2026 and D=1.
- Should be: with the 19-sheet issue of finding 1, `ceil(19/4)=5` production days + `3×3=9` bundle days + `1` non-concurrence day = **15 production days**. On the author's own date convention (BP‑3: 15 days from 31 August finishes 15 September), 31 August + 15 days = 15 September 2026; the 15‑day backcheck then runs 16–30 September 2026, which is **2 days** past the 28 September 2026 bid opening. D = 2, delay charge = `2,600×2 + 140×4 = 5,760 USD`.
- Recomputed BP‑2 ledger (17 reissued existing sheets, 2 added, 3 bundles, 1 non-concurrence, D=2, incorporated markup area 158.509 in² — see finding 3):
  - bundles 14,400.00
  - sheets (17 × 1,150 + 158.509 × 26) = 23,671.23
  - added sheets (2 × 6,400) = 12,800.00
  - revision marks (17 × 240) = 4,080.00
  - overflow Option 2 (3 × 880) = 2,640.00
  - non-concurrence = 2,400.00
  - delay = 5,760.00
  - **total = 65,751.23 USD**
  If the S‑201 transitive step is not accepted, the 18‑sheet alternative is 64,361.23 USD; either is far from the submitted 57,886.92. The author's own `requirements.csv` REQ‑011 still records "BP‑2 D=2 = 5,760 USD", corroborating the two-day result.
- Evidence: `production_rate_schedule.xlsx` A14–A17, note 4; `solicitation_schedule.csv` BP‑2 bid opening 2026‑09‑28; `design_basis.md` JSON and §4/§7. The author's 14 days is only obtainable from the incomplete 16‑sheet set.

**3. BLOCKING — the BP‑2 markup-incorporation line uses markup that is not incorporated.**
- Requirement: rate schedule A7 ("per square inch of incorporated markup extent") and note 2 ("Markup incorporation is charged on incorporated markups only. A markup that is not incorporated is charged nothing under this line"); task.md Objective.
- Deliverable has: `sheet_usd` includes 166.42 in² × 26 = 4,326.92 USD (design_basis §7).

The submitted 166.42 in² is 159.655 in² plus the S‑501 dimension markup 6.745 in² plus rounding; that S‑501 markup is EOR‑2‑019, which the register itself marks VOID (no annotation timestamp), and S‑501 is not even in the author's issue. The extra 1.146 in² S‑502 strike-out is a duplicate of the EOR‑2‑004 polygon. Both are excluded by A7/note 2. BP‑3's 182.05 in² is consistent with the valid annotations (182.034 in²).

**4. BLOCKING — the BP‑2 title-block defects omit S‑301.**
- Requirement: task.md, "Title blocks. Read the title blocks of the sheets you are re-issuing against the criteria for signing and sealing and report every sheet that does not comply, with the nature of the defect." S‑301 is one of the sheets that must be reissued under finding 1. The author's own `requirements.csv` REQ‑026 already identifies "E‑501, S‑301, A‑501, M‑101, T‑101", so the omission is internal to the final submission.
- Evidence: `.../drawings/bp2_current/74213_BP-2_S-301.pdf` production data, lines "DESIGNED BY: WKT / DRAWN BY: RCM / CHECKED BY: RCM"; `constraint_register.xlsx` RQ‑008/RQ‑009 resolutions mention only A‑501/T‑101/E‑501/M‑101.

**5. MAJOR — design-basis narrative (c) misidentifies "drawing blocks" and gives the wrong overflow cost basis.**
- Requirement: task.md Deliverable 7(c): explain "the row capacity, which option was taken, that the option is applied set-wide rather than sheet by sheet, and the cost reason the other option was rejected."

The production data shows M‑101 has one drawing block (`CHILLED WATER PLAN`), S‑101 one (`FOUNDATION PLAN`), C‑101 one, S‑102 one; the full-block sheets with three or more drawing blocks are **M‑501 (three details), S‑501 (three details) and S‑502 (four details)**. # Independent review — EOR review corrections, work order 74213

Reviewer: independent checking engineer. Subject: `/filesystem/dc_structural__eor_revision__blind/output/submission.zip` (27,032 bytes; 7 top-level files). No deliverable was modified. All values below were recomputed from the project PDFs, the markup logs, the review checklists and the published rate schedule; the author's tables and scripts were not used as evidence.

## Findings

**1. BLOCKING — the BP‑2 reference sweep is incomplete: S‑201, S‑301 and S‑501 are omitted from the issue.**
- Requirement: task.md, "What an accepted change drags in": "A change to a view forces the re-issue of every sheet that references it, and that sweep is transitive and crosses disciplines." FC 1‑300‑09N para. 18‑5.1 also requires every replaced drawing to be listed
  in the drawing index and in Document 00 01 15.
- Deliverable has: `sheet_index.csv` rows for S‑201, S‑301 and S‑501 are `CURRENT_REVISION=2`, `ISSUE_ACTION=UNCHANGED`, `IN_THIS_ISSUE=NO`; `revision_log.csv` and `issue_plan.csv` omit them; `disposition_register.csv` EOR‑2‑004 impact set is `E-101;E-501;M-101;M-102;M-301;M-401;M-501;M-502;S-102`; design_basis §7 says BP‑2 has 16 sheets (14 reissued + 2 added).
- Should be: the drawing-block callouts in the production data give S‑502 → S‑301 and S‑501; S‑301 → S‑101, S‑102 and S‑201; S‑501 → S‑101 and S‑201. The transitive closure of the changed sheets (S‑101, S‑502, M‑101, C‑101, E‑001, M‑301, M‑401, M‑501, E‑101) therefore includes S‑301, S‑501 and S‑201. The correct BP‑2 issue is **19 sheets: 17 reissued existing + 2 added** (S‑201A, M‑501A). S‑101 and S‑102 are already in the author's issue; the three missing sheets are S‑201, S‑301 and S‑501. EOR‑2‑004's impact set must also include S‑101 (dragged through S‑501/S‑301) plus S‑201, S‑301 and S‑501.
- Evidence: `.../drawings/bp2_current/74213_BP-2_S-301.pdf` production data, callouts `C S-501 DETA` and `A S-502 DETA`; `74213_BP-2_S-501.pdf`, callout `B S-502 DETA`; `74213_BP-2_S-201.pdf`, callouts `A S-501 DETA` and `1 S-301 SECT` (the same graph is reproduced in the `.txt` corpus files). The author's own design-basis method ("every sheet whose drawing block calls out a changed sheet is reissued, and that in turn draws in the sheets that call out the reissued sheet") applied consistently gives these three sheets; the author's S‑502 example stops the sweep after S‑102.

**2. BLOCKING — the BP‑2 ledger and schedule are understated (production days, delay and total cost).**
- Requirement: task.md Objective and rate schedule A5–A16; note 4 of the rate schedule defines production duration as the whole-day ceiling of sheets/4 plus 3 days per bundle plus 1 day per non-concurrence; the extension charge is `2,600 × D + 140 × D²`, `D = max(0, finish − deadline)`.
- Deliverable has: `"production_days": 14`, `"delay_days": 1`, `ledger.delay_usd=2740`, `ledger.total_usd=57886.92`; design_basis §4 says production finishes 14 September 2026 and D=1.
- Should be: with the 19-sheet issue of finding 1, `ceil(19/4)=5` production days + `3×3=9` bundle days + `1` non-concurrence day = **15 production days**. On the author's own date convention (BP‑3: 15 days from 31 August finishes 15 September), 31 August + 15 days = 15 September 2026; the 15‑day backcheck then runs 16–30 September 2026, which is **2 days** past the 28 September 2026 bid opening. D = 2, delay charge = `2,600×2 + 140×4 = 5,760 USD`.
- Recomputed BP‑2 ledger (17 reissued existing sheets, 2 added, 3 bundles, 1 non-concurrence, D=2, incorporated markup area 158.509 in² — see finding 3):
  - bundles 14,400.00
  - sheets (17 × 1,150 + 158.509 × 26) = 23,671.23
  - added sheets (2 × 6,400) = 12,800.00
  - revision marks (17 × 240) = 4,080.00 (the two added sheets are excluded because A9 says "revised sheet"; if their mark‑3 entries are charged, add 2 × 240 = 480)
  - overflow Option 2 (3 × 880) = 2,640.00
  - non-concurrence = 2,400.00
  - delay = 5,760.00
  - **total = 65,751.23 USD**
  If the S‑201 transitive step is not accepted, the 18‑sheet alternative is 64,361.23 USD; either is far from the submitted 57,886.92. The combined BP‑2 + BP‑3 cost on the corrected BP‑2 basis is 65,751.23 + 56,083.30 = **121,834.53 USD**, not the submitted 113,970.22. The author's own `requirements.csv` REQ‑011 still records "BP‑2 D=2 = 5,760 USD", corroborating the two-day result.
- Evidence: `production_rate_schedule.xlsx` A14–A17, note 4; `solicitation_schedule.csv` BP‑2 bid opening 2026‑09‑28; `design_basis.md` JSON and §4/§7. The author's 14 days is only obtainable from the incomplete 16‑sheet set. If one instead counts the start day inclusively, the 15‑day BP‑3 finish would be 14 September, not the 15 September stated in design_basis §3; the submission cannot use both conventions. Under the author's stated BP‑3 convention the BP‑2 D is 2.

**3. BLOCKING — the BP‑2 markup-incorporation line uses markup that is not incorporated.**
- Requirement: rate schedule A7 ("per square inch of incorporated markup extent") and note 2 ("Markup incorporation is charged on incorporated markups only. A markup that is not incorporated is charged nothing under this line"); task.md Objective.
- Deliverable has: `sheet_usd` includes 166.42 in² × 26 = 4,326.92 USD (design_basis §7).
- Should be: the valid CONCUR annotations total **158.509 in²** = 4,121.23 USD (or 159.655 in² = 4,151.02 USD if the red S‑502 strike-out is counted as part of EOR‑2‑004). The submitted 166.42 in² is 159.655 in² plus the S‑501 dimension markup 6.745 in² plus rounding; that S‑501 markup is EOR‑2‑019, which the register itself marks VOID (no annotation timestamp), and S‑501 is not even in the author's issue. The extra 1.146 in² S‑502 strike-out is a duplicate of the EOR‑2‑004 polygon. Both are excluded by A7/note 2. BP‑3's 182.05 in² is consistent with the valid annotations (182.034 in²).
- Evidence: PDF annotation rectangles measured in points at 72 pt/in: C‑101 25.858, E‑001 13.000, E‑101 9.600, M‑101 16.434, M‑301 19.291 + 6.400, M‑401 18.811, S‑101 10.772 + 12.521, S‑502 25.822 (+1.146 strike-out); S‑501 6.745 has blank creation date and is EOR‑2‑019 VOID. `disposition_register.csv` EOR‑2‑019 `VALIDITY=VOID`, `SHEETS_CHANGED` blank.

**4. BLOCKING — the BP‑2 title-block defects omit S‑301.**
- Requirement: task.md, "Title blocks. Read the title blocks of the sheets you are re-issuing against the criteria for signing and sealing and report every sheet that does not comply, with the nature of the defect." FC 1‑300‑09N para. 12‑4.1: "The CHK initials CANNOT be the same as the DES and DRW initials."

- Should be: include **S‑301 with `CHK_EQUALS_DRW`**. S‑301's title block reads `DESIGNED BY: WKT`, `DRAWN BY: RCM`, `CHECKED BY: RCM` — CHK equals DRW. S‑301 is one of the sheets that must be reissued under finding 1. The author's own `requirements.csv` REQ‑026 already identifies "E‑501, S‑301, A‑501, M‑101, T‑101", so the omission is internal to the final submission.
- Evidence: `.../drawings/bp2_current/74213_BP-2_S-301.pdf` production data, lines "DESIGNED BY: WKT / DRAWN BY: RCM / CHECKED BY: RCM"; `constraint_register.xlsx` RQ‑008/RQ‑009 resolutions mention only A‑501/T‑101/E‑501/M‑101.

**5. MAJOR — design-basis narrative (c) misidentifies "drawing blocks" and gives the wrong overflow cost basis.**
- Requirement: task.md Deliverable 7(c): explain "the row capacity, which option was taken, that the option is applied set-wide rather than sheet by sheet, and the cost reason the other option was rejected."

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
import sys, os, csv, json, math, datetime, shutil

import model as m
from comments import C
from data import SHEETS, ADDED
import titleblocks

OUT='/tmp/ahpele/work/out'
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

ADDED_BY={'EOR-2-023':'M-501A','EOR-2-025':'S-201A','EOR-3-024':'A-402','EOR-3-026':'M-502'}
SHEETINFO={}
for p in SHEETS:
    for s in SHEETS[p]: SHEETINFO[(p,s[0])]=s
    for a in ADDED[p]: SHEETINFO[(p,a[0])]=(a[0],a[1],a[2],a[3],'',a[4],0,0)

def mk(cid):
    p='BP-2' if '-2-' in cid else 'BP-3'
    return 'MK-%s-%s'%({'BP-2':'2','BP-3':'3'}[p], cid.split('-')[-1])

for cid,d in C.items():
    pkg='BP-2' if '-2-' in cid else 'BP-3'
    d['pkg']=pkg
    ch=set(); ad=set()
    if d['validity']=='VALID' and d['resp']=='CONCUR':
        ch.add(d['sheet'])
        if cid in ADDED_BY: ad.add(ADDED_BY[cid])
    d['added']=sorted(ad); d['changed_base']=sorted(ch); d['changed']=sorted(ch|ad)
    d['impacted']=sorted(m.closure(m.BP2 if pkg=='BP-2' else m.BP3, ch)-ch) if ch else []
    if ad: d['impacted']=sorted(set(d['impacted'])|{'GI-001'})

ISSUE={}
for pkg in ('BP-2','BP-3'):
    sheets=set(); added=set()
    for cid,d in C.items():
        if d['pkg']!=pkg: continue
        sheets |= set(d['changed_base']) | set(d['impacted'])
        added |= set(d['added'])
    ISSUE[pkg]=(sorted(sheets), sorted(added))

BUNDLES={
 'BP-2':[['M-101','M-102','M-301','M-401','M-501'],
         ['S-101','S-102','S-201A','S-502'],
         ['C-101','E-001','E-101','E-501','M-501A','M-502','GI-001']],
 'BP-3':[['A-001','A-101','A-102','A-201','A-301','A-401','A-402','A-501','A-502'],
         ['S-101','S-102','S-301','S-501','M-101','M-301','M-501','M-502'],
         ['E-101','E-102','E-501','T-101','T-501','GI-001']],
}
BFILE={'BP-2':['74213Amend0003dwg1of3.pdf','74213Amend0003dwg2of3.pdf','74213Amend0003dwg3of3.pdf'],
       'BP-3':['74213dwg1of3.pdf','74213dwg2of3.pdf','74213dwg3of3.pdf']}
ORDER={'BP-2':['G-001','GI-001','GI-002','C-101','C-102','C-301','C-501',
               'S-001','S-002','S-101','S-102','S-201','S-201A','S-301','S-501','S-502',
               'M-001','M-002','M-003','M-101','M-102','M-301','M-401','M-501','M-501A','M-502',
               'E-001','E-002','E-004','E-101','E-501'],
       'BP-3':['G-001','GI-001','A-001','A-002','A-101','A-102','A-201','A-301','A-401','A-402','A-501','A-502',
               'S-101','S-102','S-301','S-501','M-101','M-301','M-501','M-502',
               'E-101','E-102','E-501','T-101','T-501']}

def mb(pkg,s): return SHEETINFO[(pkg,s)][5]
LEDGER={}; DETAIL={}
for pkg in ('BP-2','BP-3'):
    sheets,added=ISSUE[pkg]
    allb=sum(BUNDLES[pkg],[])
    assert set(allb)==set(sheets)|set(added), (pkg,set(allb)^(set(sheets)|set(added)))
    assert len(allb)==len(set(allb))
    for b in BUNDLES[pkg]:
        assert sum(mb(pkg,s) for s in b)<=50.0+1e-9, (pkg,b,sum(mb(pkg,s) for s in b))
    nb=len(BUNDLES[pkg]); n=len(sheets)+len(added)
    nc=sum(1 for cid,d in C.items() if d['pkg']==pkg and d['resp']=='NON_CONCUR')
    area=sum(m.M[mk(cid)]['area'] for cid,d in C.items() if d['pkg']==pkg and d['validity']=='VALID' and d['resp']=='CONCUR')
    prod=math.ceil(n/4)+3*nb+nc
    start=datetime.date(2026,8,31); fin=start+datetime.timedelta(days=prod)
    if pkg=='BP-2': deadline=datetime.date(2026,9,28); window=15; amend=True
    else: deadline=datetime.date(2026,11,9); window=30; amend=False
    D=max(0,(fin-deadline).days+window)
    bundles_usd=nb*4800
    nre=len(sheets)
    sheets_usd=round(nre*1150+area*26,2)
    added_usd=len(added)*6400
    marks_usd=nre*240 if amend else 0
    if amend:
        full=[s for s in sheets if SHEETINFO[(pkg,s)][6]==8]
        ov2=[s for s in full if SHEETINFO[(pkg,s)][7]>=3]
        overflow=880*len(ov2); overflow_opt=2
    else:
        overflow=0; overflow_opt='NONE'
    nc_usd=nc*2400; delay=2600*D+140*D*D
    total=round(bundles_usd+sheets_usd+added_usd+marks_usd+overflow+nc_usd+delay,2)
    LEDGER[pkg]=dict(bundles_usd=bundles_usd,sheets_usd=sheets_usd,added_sheets_usd=added_usd,
                     revision_marks_usd=marks_usd,overflow_option_usd=overflow,non_concurrence_usd=nc_usd,
                     delay_usd=delay,total_usd=total)
    defects=[]
    for s in sheets+added:
        if (pkg,s) not in titleblocks.TB: continue
        tb=titleblocks.TB[(pkg,s)]
        for k in ('CHK_EQUALS_DES','CHK_EQUALS_DRW','SEAL_DISCIPLINE_MISMATCH'):
            if tb[k]: defects.append({'sheet':s,'defect':k})
    DETAIL[pkg]=dict(issue_state='AMENDMENT' if amend else 'PRE_ADVERTISEMENT_REISSUE',
                     change_number='0003' if amend else '', overflow_option=overflow_opt,
                     revision_layers=['Z-ANNO-REVC','Z-ANNO-REVS'], n_bundles=nb, production_days=prod,
                     delay_days=D, backcheck_window_days=window, ledger=LEDGER[pkg], title_block_defects=defects)
    DETAIL[pkg]['_n']=n; DETAIL[pkg]['_nre']=nre; DETAIL[pkg]['_nc']=nc; DETAIL[pkg]['_area']=round(area,2); DETAIL[pkg]['_finish']=str(fin)
    DETAIL[pkg]['_sheets']=sheets; DETAIL[pkg]['_added']=added

# ---------- disposition_register.csv
cols=['PACKAGE','COMMENT_ID','AUTHOR','SIGNIFICANCE','VALIDITY','VOID_REASON','RESPONSE','RESOLUTION',
      'PRIMARY_SHEET','PRIMARY_VIEW','CHANGE_KIND','SHEETS_CHANGED','SHEETS_IMPACTED','CLOSURE']
with open(os.path.join(OUT,'disposition_register.csv'),'w',newline='') as f:
    w=csv.DictWriter(f,fieldnames=cols); w.writeheader()
    for cid in sorted(C, key=lambda x:(C[x]['pkg'],x)):
        d=C[cid]
        w.writerow(dict(PACKAGE=d['pkg'],COMMENT_ID=cid,AUTHOR=d['author'],SIGNIFICANCE=d['sig'],
            VALIDITY=d['validity'],VOID_REASON=d['void'],RESPONSE=d['resp'],RESOLUTION=d['res'],
            PRIMARY_SHEET=d['sheet'],PRIMARY_VIEW=d['view'],CHANGE_KIND=d['kind'],
            SHEETS_CHANGED=';'.join(d['changed']),SHEETS_IMPACTED=';'.join(d['impacted']),CLOSURE=d['closure']))

# ---------- sheet_index.csv
with open(os.path.join(OUT,'sheet_index.csv'),'w',newline='') as f:
    w=csv.writer(f); w.writerow(['PACKAGE','INDEX_ORDER','SHEET_NUMBER','SHEET_NAME','CURRENT_REVISION','ISSUE_ACTION','IN_THIS_ISSUE'])
    for pkg in ('BP-2','BP-3'):
        sheets,added=ISSUE[pkg]
        for i,s in enumerate(ORDER[pkg],1):
            info=SHEETINFO[(pkg,s)]
            if s in added: act='ADD'; rev='3' if pkg=='BP-2' else ''
            elif s in sheets: act='REPLACE'; rev='3' if pkg=='BP-2' else info[4]
            else: act='UNCHANGED'; rev=info[4]
            w.writerow([pkg,i,s,info[1],rev,act,'YES' if (s in sheets or s in added) else 'NO'])

# ---------- revision_log.csv
with open(os.path.join(OUT,'revision_log.csv'),'w',newline='') as f:
    w=csv.writer(f); w.writerow(['PACKAGE','SHEET_NUMBER','MARK','DESCRIPTION','DATE','ROW_POSITION','OVERFLOW_OPTION'])
    for pkg in ('BP-2','BP-3'):

            if s not in sheets and s not in added: continue
            info=SHEETINFO[(pkg,s)]
            if pkg=='BP-2':

def mkid(pkg,c):

def plan(pkg, inc_prefs, void=(), nb=None, discipline=False, window=None, deadline=None, lead=None):
    changed=set(CHG[pkg][c] for c in DIRECTIVE[pkg])
    added=set()
    for c in DIRECTIVE[pkg]:
        if mkid(pkg,c) in ADD[pkg]: added.add(ADD[pkg][mkid(pkg,c)])
    area={}

    nonconc=[]
    for c in PREF[pkg]:

        if c in inc_prefs:
            changed.add(CHG[pkg][c]); area[CHG[pkg][c]]=area.get(CHG[pkg][c],0)+M[mkid(pkg,c)]['area']
        else:
            nonconc.append(c)
    ch=set(changed); imp=m.closure(m.BP2 if pkg=='BP-2' else m.BP3, ch)
    sheets=ch|imp
    mb=sum(m.PLOT[(pkg,s)] for s in sheets)+5.5*len(added)

    # min bundles by pure size
    nbmin=math.ceil((mb-1e-9)/50)
    prod=math.ceil(n/4)+3*(nb if nb else nbmin)+len(nonconc)
    fin=datetime.date(2026,8,31)+datetime.timedelta(days=prod)
    D=max(0,(fin-deadline).days+window)
    delay=2600*D+140*D*D
    return dict(changed=sorted(changed),impacted=sorted(imp),sheets=sorted(sheets),added=sorted(added),n=n,mb=round(mb,1),nb=nb or nbmin,prod=prod,fin=str(fin),D=D,delay=delay,nonconc=sorted(nonconc),area=area)

if __name__=='__main__':
    for pkg,deadline,window in [('BP-2',datetime.date(2026,9,28),15),('BP-3',datetime.date(2026,11,9),30)]:
        print('=====',pkg)
        base=plan(pkg,[],deadline=deadline,window=window)
        print('directives only:',{k:base[k] for k in ('changed','impacted','added','n','mb','nb','prod','fin','D','delay')})
        for r in range(len(PREF[pkg])+1):
            for combo in itertools.combinations(PREF[pkg],r):

## 1. Documents that govern, and documents set aside

The governing design procedures criteria is FC 1-300-09N, 17 May 2024 with Change 1 of 17 April 2025. Its paragraph 12-3.3.4 fixes the order of precedence for CAD standards: the requirements of its own Chapter 12 come first, then the latest releases of the DoD A/E/C CAD Standard and the A/E/C Graphics Standard, then the National CAD Standard. The current releases in the project file are the A/E/C CAD Standard Release 6.2 (ERDC/ITL SR-24-3) and the A/E/C Graphics Standard Release 2.2 (ERDC/ITL SR-23-1).

Set aside: UFC 1-300-09N (2005, Change 7) is cancelled and is superseded by the FC; the A/E/C CAD Standard Release 6.0 (TR-12-6) is superseded by Release 6.2; the A/E/C Graphics Standard Release 2.1 is superseded by Release 2.2; the GSA PBS CAD Standard 2021 is another agency standard; the fire protection comment log belongs to a separate A-E task order and discipline; and the superseded 90 percent and 60 percent prints are not the issue any change is made against.

The Contracting Officer memorandum of 26 August 2026 adopts ER 1165-2-217 and the markup and record-package conventions of ERDC/ITL SR-21-6 for this work order. ER 415-1-11 governs the timing of the review backcheck. FAR 52.236-25 requires that design work be prepared, reviewed and approved by registered professionals in the particular professional field involved, which is the basis of the seal findings below.

## 2. Revision-graphics layer conflict resolved (item a)

The two shipped documents that disagree are FC 1-300-09N and the A/E/C CAD Standard Release 6.2. FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-3.6.1 places revision clouds on layer Z-ANNO-REVC and revision symbols, notes and revision-block entries on layer Z-ANNO-REVS. The A/E/C CAD Standard Release 6.2 assigns the same two functions to G-ANNO-REVC and G-ANNO-REVS. The clause that fixes the order of precedence is FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-3.3.4: the requirements of its own Chapter 12 rank ahead of the A/E/C CAD Standard and the A/E/C Graphics Standard, which in turn rank ahead of the National CAD Standard. The revision-graphics requirement sits in the FC Chapter 12, so the FC prevails and the layers actually used for every revised sheet in this issue are Z-ANNO-REVC (clouds) and Z-ANNO-REVS (revision triangles, indicators, notes and the Revision (Issue) block entries). The A/E/C CAD Standard G-ANNO-REVC and G-ANNO-REVS layer names were not used. Every revised sheet therefore carries its change clouded on Z-ANNO-REVC with an equilateral triangle numbered 3 beside the cloud, and the Revision (Issue) block entry and note text on Z-ANNO-REVS; the two added sheets carry the same mark 3 with the description SHEET ADDED IN ACCORDANCE WITH AMDT 0003.

## 3. BP-3 issue state (item b)

BP-3 has not been advertised. The solicitation schedule export shows a scheduled advertisement of 12 October 2026, but the later Contracting Officer memorandum of 26 August 2026 states that BP-3 is scheduled to advertise on 9 November 2026; the memorandum is the later dated instrument and controls, so the advertisement date used is 9 November 2026 and the bid opening date remains 12 November 2026.

The review regulation is ER 415-1-11. It gives two durations. Its paragraph g requires the backcheck to be started 30 calendar days before advertising and requires all comments to be resolved before bid opening or proposal evaluation. Its paragraph e, subparagraph (4) allows about 15 calendar days for backchecking of comments. For a package whose corrections are incorporated before advertisement, the 30-day window binds, because the backcheck must precede the advertisement itself. The 15-day period is the backcheck allowance that binds when corrections are issued as an amendment after advertisement, where resolution must precede bid opening.

Production of the BP-3 corrections takes 15 calendar days from the 31 August 2026 start (23 sheets at 4 sheets per calendar day, rounded up to 6 days, plus 3 bundles at 3 days each, with no non-concurrence days) and finishes on 15 September 2026. That is 55 days before the 9 November 2026 advertisement, so the 30-day backcheck window (which opens on 10 October 2026) is comfortably met and the advertisement date does not move. The title block ISSUE DATE on the BP-3 sheets becomes NOVEMBER 2026, the month of advertisement (the BP-2 sheets keep JULY 2026, their advertisement month, and are distinguished by the new revision-block date). BP-3 is therefore issued as a pre-advertisement reissue of the corrected design, not as an amendment: no change number is assigned, no continuation sheet is submitted, no revision-block entry is made, sheets are resequenced and the two added sheets are numbered A-402 and M-502. The alternative course, advertising on 9 November and amending afterwards, was rejected because it would add revision marks and revision-block overflow charges for no schedule gain and would require a continuation sheet and a change number that the pre-advertisement course avoids.

## 4. BP-2 issue state and Revision (Issue) block overflow (item c)

BP-2 was advertised on 6 July 2026 and its bid opening is 28 September 2026, so the only lawful issue state is an amendment to the solicitation. Two amendments have already been issued, so the next number in numerical order, in the three-cipher form required by FC 1-300-09N paragraph 18-3, is 0003. The amendment is documented on a continuation sheet with the Standard Form 30 coversheet, and the 15-day backcheck period of ER 415-1-11 paragraph e, subparagraph (4) applies: production finishes on 14 September 2026, the backcheck opens on 15 September 2026 and takes 15 calendar days, so it cannot be complete before the 28 September 2026 bid opening. The bid opening therefore moves 1 calendar day to 29 September 2026 and the extension charge is 2,600 x 1 + 140 x 1 = 2,740.00 USD.

The Revision (Issue) block provided by the A/E/C Graphics Standard holds eight rows. Six of the BP-2 sheets in this issue already carry eight entries: C-101, M-101, M-501, S-101, S-102, S-502. The graphics standard offers two overflow options and requires the chosen option to be used consistently across the whole set. Option 1 (replace the oldest entry, 520 USD per revised full sheet) would cost 6 x 520 = 3,120 USD. Option 2 (spill above the eighth row, 880 USD per revised full sheet that carries three or more drawing blocks, nothing where the spill area is unoccupied) is charged only on M-101 and S-101, which carry three drawing blocks each, and costs 2 x 880 = 1,760 USD; the other 4 full sheets have fewer than three drawing blocks and cost nothing. Option 2 was adopted set-wide and Option 1 was rejected on cost: 3,120 USD against 1,760 USD, a saving of 1,360 USD, with the spill confined to the unoccupied area above the block on the three-block sheets. The option is applied to every revised sheet in the set, not sheet by sheet, and the new entry is placed above the existing entries (row 9 on the full sheets, the next free row on the others).

## 5. Disposition method, void markups and non-concurrence

Of the 34 comments, 17 are directive design or coordination findings and are all incorporated; 8 markups cannot direct a change and are closed void or closed by elevation; 1 non-directive comment is answered by a documented non-concurrence; and 8 non-directive preferences are adopted because adoption costs less than the non-concurrence charge. The disposition register carries the response, resolution and every changed and impacted location for each comment.

Every comment in the two EOR markup logs was assessed against the four-part comment convention of ER 1165-2-217 paragraph 5.8.3 and answered with the three-part response of paragraph 5.8.7 (concur or non-concur, how the comment is resolved, and every location affected). Where a markup cannot direct a change it was closed as void with the ground stated, and no sheet was changed for it:

- EOR-2-017 - Author is not listed on the reviewer roster for this review, so the markup is not a review comment and cannot direct a design change.
- EOR-2-019 - The markup annotation carries no creation timestamp, so it cannot be shown to have been made within the review period or authenticated as a review comment; it cannot direct a change.
- EOR-2-021 - The markup is drawn on the superseded 90 percent submittal print of S-102, which is not the current issue and is not the issue any change is made against.
- EOR-2-033 - Closed in the 60 percent review with a notation that it was elevated for resolution; that closure was never reopened, so the markup cannot direct a further change.
- EOR-3-012 - The markup is drawn on the superseded 60 percent submittal print of T-501, which is not the current issue and is not the issue any change is made against.
- EOR-3-020 - The markup annotation carries no creation timestamp, so it cannot be shown to have been made within the review period or authenticated as a review comment; it cannot direct a change.
- EOR-3-022 - Author is not listed on the reviewer roster for this review, so the markup is not a review comment and cannot direct a design change.
- EOR-3-036 - Closed in the 60 percent review with a notation that it was elevated for resolution; that closure was never reopened, so the markup cannot direct a further change.

Six yellow text notes reading CHECKED - NO COMMENT (K. Aoyama) are participation notes with no comment record, and the four fire protection comments in the other-discipline log belong to a separate A-E task order; none is an EOR review comment of BP-2 or BP-3, so none is carried into the disposition register. The markup colour convention of ERDC/ITL SR-21-6 distinguishes additions (green), deletions (red) and items requiring clarification (blue); the blue markups are the non-directive preferences. Under ER 1165-2-217 paragraph 5.8.5 a comment that only enforces a personal preference is not directive. Each non-directive comment was priced both ways and the cheaper lawful course taken. EOR-2-011 (bearing area table relocation) is documented as a non-concurrence because adopting it would draw in three civil sheets that are not otherwise in the issue, at 4,347 USD, against 2,400 USD for the documented non-concurrence plus one processing day; the arrangement as drawn is legible and has no code basis for change. The other non-directive markups were adopted because they cost less than a non-concurrence: most sit on sheets this issue already reissues and cost only the markup extent (26 USD per square inch, roughly 170 to 250 USD each), and the one that draws in a new sheet (EOR-2-013 on E-001) costs 1,728 USD including the reissue and revision mark. Both are far below the 2,400 USD non-concurrence charge plus a processing day that would also have pushed the finish date.

Reference sweep. The reference graph was read from the drawing-block callouts printed in the production data of each sheet. A callout for a detail must point to a 5-series sheet, an enlarged area to a 4-series sheet, a section to a 3-series sheet and an elevation to a 2-series sheet (A/E/C Graphics Standard paragraphs 4.2.4.2 to 4.2.4.4); every callout in both sets was checked against those couplings. Reissue was propagated transitively in the reverse direction: every sheet whose drawing block calls out a changed sheet is reissued, and that in turn draws in the sheets that call out the reissued sheet. The BP-2 change to the equipment anchorage on S-502, for example, reaches E-501, M-501, M-502, S-102 and then M-102, M-301, M-101, M-401 and E-101; the BP-3 change to the structural details on S-501 reaches eighteen other sheets across five disciplines.

## 6. Title block findings

Each sheet in the two issues was read against FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-4.1: the CHK initials may not be the same as the DES or DRW initials, and the electronic seal must be that of the discipline responsible for the sheet, consistent with FAR 52.236-25. The non-compliant sheets are:

- BP-2 E-501 - seal is for a different discipline than the sheet content
- BP-3 A-501 - CHECKED BY initials equal DESIGNED BY initials
- BP-3 M-101 - seal is for a different discipline than the sheet content
- BP-3 T-101 - CHECKED BY initials equal DRAWN BY initials

These are corrected on the reissued sheets before signature and seal: the CHK initials are assigned to a checker other than the designer or drafter, and the seal is replaced with the seal of the discipline responsible for the sheet (electrical for E-501 in BP-2, mechanical for M-101 in BP-3). Sheets not in the issue were not reissued and their defects are not charged to this issue, but C-102 in BP-2 carries the same CHK-equals-DES condition and should be corrected at the next reissue.

## 7. Issue content, packaging and cost

**BP-2** - AMENDMENT. 16 sheets in the issue (14 reissued, 2 added), 3 bundles. Ledger: bundles $14,400.00; sheets including markup incorporation $20,426.92; added sheets $12,800.00; revision marks $3,360.00; overflow option $1,760.00; non-concurrence $2,400.00; delay $2,740.00; total $57,886.92 USD.

**BP-3** - PRE_ADVERTISEMENT_REISSUE. 23 sheets in the issue (21 reissued, 2 added), 3 bundles. Ledger: bundles $14,400.00; sheets including markup incorporation $28,883.30; added sheets $12,800.00; revision marks $0.00; overflow option $0.00; non-concurrence $0.00; delay $0.00; total $56,083.30 USD.

Bundling observes the 50 MB drawing-PDF limit of FC 1-300-09N paragraph 12-3.5.1. Each bundle is at or below 50 MB and complete discipline sets are kept whole wherever they fit, as paragraph 12-3.5.2.1 requires. In BP-2 the mechanical set alone exceeds 50 MB, so it is the only discipline split, into two parts, and no discipline set is otherwise broken. In BP-3 the architectural set fills one bundle and the structural and mechanical sets share the second; the electrical and telecommunications sets share the third. Every bundle is bookmarked by discipline and by sheet, and the sheets are signed and sealed before delivery per paragraph 12-3.5.2.
